READ-ONLY. I am auditing a client-facing "outstanding actions awaiting Zimmermann" list. Your job is to find whether specific DECISIONS/QUESTIONS are already ANSWERED/CONFIRMED, or still OPEN, in the project docs. Report FILE PATH + LINE NUMBERS and quote the relevant text for each.

Read these files under /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/ :
- .docs/vendor/didomi.md, .docs/vendor/measmerize.md, .docs/vendor/optimizely.md, .docs/vendor/global-e.md, .docs/vendor/giveX.md, .docs/vendor/mulesoft.md, .docs/vendor/sparroSchema.md
- .docs/prd/regional.md, .docs/prd/analytics.md, .docs/prd/giftcards.md, .docs/prd/pdp.md, .docs/prd/pricing-currency-globale.md

Determine the current status (CONFIRMED / DECIDED / STILL-OPEN / CONTRADICTORY) of EACH of these specific questions, with path:line evidence and a short quote:

1. Consent approach for MEASMERIZE — "load freely + call disable-APIs when consent denied" vs "gate whole script behind a Didomi category". Decided or open?
2. Consent approach for VIMEO — "append dnt=1 (no gate)" vs "gate behind Didomi category". Decided or open?
3. VIDEO PLATFORM confirmation (PRD-067) — is Vimeo confirmed as the video platform, or still open?
4. DIDOMI consent categories (Performance/Analytics/Marketing) purpose/vendor IDs — provided or still needed? Any category confirmed for reCAPTCHA, Narvar, Optimizely, Crazy Egg?
5. LOGIN MFA — in scope for launch or post-launch, or undecided?
6. CONTENT OWNERSHIP Contentful vs SFCC — the `regions` content-model field sign-off, and PDP/PLP/category/mega-menu editorial split. Decided or open?
7. GIFT-CARD PROVIDER for Global-e international checkout — GiveX vs Adyen vs SFCC-native. Decided or open? (raised by Global-e 26 Jun)
8. BOOKSY vs BOOXI — are they confirmed to be the same appointments vendor, or is it noted as an unresolved naming question?
9. BOOXI scope — read-only appointment history vs in-storefront booking/reschedule/cancel; which sprint. Decided or open?
10. GiveX balance-check CAPTCHA — decided whether the balance-check route presents a CAPTCHA? 
11. CRAZY EGG masking ownership (Tell No Lies owns/applies masking) — confirmed or open?
12. GTM / Addingwell — is the prod tagging-server host confirmed (e.g. ruffles.zimmermann.com)? Are non-prod hosts still needed? Does the GTM container load via Addingwell?
13. ZENDESK, KLARNA, ZENKRAFT/ZENCRAFT — any mention? Are they in/out of Accenture build scope? Is Zenkraft-vs-Zencraft flagged as a naming question?

Be exhaustive and precise with line numbers. Quote sparingly but exactly. Do not edit anything.

1	> Source (from Didomi, 15 Jun 2026): https://developers.didomi.io/cmp/web-sdk/getting-started
2	
3	
4	React package: https://github.com/didomi/react
5	
6	---
7	
8	## Installation
9	
10	```bash
11	npm install --save @didomi/react
12	```
13	
14	## DidomiSDK component
15	
16	Mount once, as high in the tree as possible (e.g. `_app.tsx`):
17	
18	```tsx
19	import { DidomiSDK } from '@didomi/react'
20	
21	<DidomiSDK
22	  apiKey="YOUR_API_KEY"
23	  iabVersion={2}
24	  gdprAppliesGlobally={true}
25	  onReady={(didomi) => { /* store ref; fire consent-gated scripts */ }}
26	  onConsentChanged={(cwtToken) => { /* re-evaluate consent gates */ }}
27	/>
28	```
29	
30	| Key prop | Notes |
31	|---|---|
32	| `apiKey` | Zimmermann to provide (one per environment, or shared — TBC) |
33	| `noticeId` | Alternative to `apiKey` when targeting a specific notice |
34	| `gdprAppliesGlobally` | Set `true` to show banner to all users, not EU-only |
35	| `embedTCFStub` | Defaults `true` — embeds IAB TCF stub before SDK loads |
36	| `country` / `region` | ISO overrides; useful for storefront-aware consent logic |
37	
38	Full callback list: `onNoticeShown`, `onNoticeHidden`, `onNoticeClickAgree`, `onPreferencesClickAgreeToAll`, `onPreferencesClickPurposeAgree(purposeId)`, `onPreferencesClickVendorAgree(vendorId)`, etc.
39	
40	## Checking consent programmatically
41	
42	The `didomi` object from `onReady` (and re-evaluated in `onConsentChanged`):
43	
44	```ts
45	didomi.isConsentRequired()
46	didomi.getUserConsentStatusForVendor(vendorId)   // true | false | undefined
47	didomi.getUserConsentStatus(purposeId, vendorId) // true | false | undefined
48	```
49	
50	Fail closed: if the result is `undefined` (undetermined), treat as denied — do not load the third-party script.
51	
52	## TypeScript
53	
54	Full TypeScript support via `index.d.ts` included in the package.

1	# Optimizely Web Experimentation — Vendor Reference
2	
3	> Source: Zimmermann-provided link (received 2026-06-10)
4	> https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/4411731640973-Implement-the-one-line-JavaScript-snippet
5	> Article last updated: 2025-12-17
6	
7	Applies to: **Optimizely Web Experimentation** and Optimizely Personalization.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Zimmermann project snippet
12	
13	Confirmed by Zimmermann 2026-06-10. US storefront only.
14	
15	```html
16	<script src="https://cdn.optimizely.com/js/4599769641779200.js"></script>
17	```
18	
19	- **Project ID:** `4599769641779200` (the number preceding `.js` in the URL)
20	- One snippet; single project covers all environments per Zimmermann confirmation.
21	
22	---
23	
24	## Placement
25	
26	Add the snippet as **high in the `<head>` as possible**, immediately after charset/meta declarations:
27	
28	```html
29	<!DOCTYPE html>
30	<html lang="en">
31	  <head>
32	    <meta http-equiv="Content-Type" content="text/html; charset=utf-8">
33	    <!-- other meta tags -->
34	    <!-- stylesheets -->
35	    <script src="https://cdn.optimizely.com/js/4599769641779200.js"></script>
36	    <!-- all other scripts and content -->
37	  </head>
38	  <body>
39	```
40	
41	**Place BEFORE the snippet:**
42	- Charset declarations and other meta tags
43	- jQuery (if using your own version, not Optimizely's)
44	
45	**Place AFTER the snippet:**
46	- All other page elements
47	- Analytics or heatmapping code (e.g. Crazy Egg, GTM)
48	- Other tag manager content
49	
50	**Why:** Optimizely works by transforming the page as it loads. If anything renders before the snippet executes, visitors briefly see the original page — known as **page flashing**. Head-first placement eliminates this.
51	
52	---
53	
54	## Loading mode
55	
56	The snippet loads **synchronously by default**. This is the recommended mode for anti-flicker. Asynchronous loading is possible but not recommended for experimentation — see Optimizely's "Synchronous and asynchronous snippet loading" article if required.
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Do not use a tag manager
61	
62	> "You should not load the Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet through a tag manager."
63	
64	Google Tag Manager does not support synchronous loading, which causes page flashing and analytics integration issues. Load the snippet **directly in the page `<head>`**, outside of GTM. (This is already the agreed architecture for this project — see integration doc `15-optimizely.md`.)
65	
66	---
67	
68	## React / SSR considerations
69	
70	For server-side rendering and hydration (applicable to this PWA), Optimizely's developer docs cover how to prevent the snippet from auto-executing server-side and how to reduce flickering. See the Solutions section of Optimizely's React SSR and hydration documentation (linked from the article above).
71	
72	The PWA implementation must inject the snippet only on the client side (post-hydration or via a `<Script>` tag with appropriate strategy), to avoid SSR execution while still placing it early in the `<head>` for the browser.
73	
74	---
75	
76	## Origins
77	
78	Specify the domains where Optimizely runs and tracks events in the Optimizely project settings. An origin is a combination of hostname, protocol, and port. Cross-origin event tracking requires cross-origin targeting to be enabled in the project. Zimmermann to confirm origin configuration for US storefront domains (production + non-production).
79	
80	---
81	
82	## Key rules
83	
84	- Never use more than one snippet on the same site at a time.
85	- Do not modify the snippet — copy it exactly as provided.
86	- The snippet auto-updates; the `<script src>` tag does not need to be changed when experiments change.
87	- If separate dev/prod environments or different domains need isolation, separate Optimizely projects (and separate snippets) are required. However, Zimmermann has confirmed a single snippet for all environments.
88

1	# Global-e SFCC Integration Guide — PWA-relevant extracts
2	
3	Source: *Global-e SFCC Integration Guide v24.5.0 (SFRA v7.0.0)*
4	
5	Only sections that directly inform PWA implementation are reproduced here.
6	SFCC-side cartridge installation, BM configuration, jobs, and services are omitted.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## Checkout flow (headless / PWA)
11	
12	The Global-e checkout lives inside an **iframe** served from Global-e servers.
13	The PWA (parent frame) hosts a container route that loads the iframe.
14	
15	Steps in order:
16	
17	1. **Reserve inventory** — SFCC calls `basket.reserveInventory()` before posting the cart
18	   to Global-e (configurable; default hold time: 30 minutes).
19	
20	2. **SendCart API** — The PWA calls SFCC, which posts the complete basket to Global-e.
21	   The response is a `cartToken` representing the cloned cart on Global-e's side.
22	
23	3. **Show checkout** — The PWA renders the Global-e checkout inside an iframe using the
24	   `cartToken`.
25	
26	4. **ValidateCart** — When the shopper clicks "Place Order" inside the iframe, Global-e
27	   calls the SFCC `Globale-ValidateCart` endpoint to check stock against SFCC inventory.
28	   - If stock is insufficient the shopper sees a popup and is redirected to the cart.
29	     No order is created on either side.
30	   - This endpoint can be extended via the `globale.validateCart` custom hook.
31	
32	5. **Order creation (postMessage)** — After the order is confirmed inside the iframe,
33	   Global-e sends a `postMessage` to the parent frame. The parent frame makes an AJAX
34	   request to `orderCreate()` on SFCC, which converts the basket to an SFCC order.
35	   - The order is created with status **Created**.
36	   - Creation can fail due to session expiry, stock issues, or basket changes.
37	     In that case Global-e's retry mechanism recreates the basket from stored data
38	     and places the order via the fallback `SendOrderToMerchant` path.
39	
40	6. **SendOrderToMerchant API** — Global-e calls SFCC seconds later to enrich the order
41	   with full international transaction data. Order status moves to **New**.
42	
43	7. **PerformPayment API** — After fraud screening passes, Global-e calls SFCC.
44	   Order payment status → **Paid**; export status → **Ready for Export**.
45	
46	---
47	
48	## SFCC session custom attributes written by Global-e
49	
50	These are available on every storefront request after Global-e initialisation.
51	
52	| Attribute | Type | Description | Default | Example |
53	|---|---|---|---|---|
54	| `geCountry` | String | Currently selected/detected country (ISO2) | — | `GB` |
55	| `geIsOperated` | Boolean | Whether this country is operated by Global-e | `false` | `true` |
56	| `geCurrency` | String | Currency ISO3 code for the selected country | — | `GBP` |
57	| `gePriceStrategy` | String | Pricing strategy for the country | `DYNAMIC` | `FIXED` / `DYNAMIC` |
58	| `geCulture` | String | BCP 47 culture/locale code for the selected country | — | `en-GB` |
59	| `geApiVersion` | String | Global-e API version in use | — | `2.1.4` |
60	
61	---
62	
63	## GlobalE_Data cookie
64	
65	Global-e sets a cookie named `GlobalE_Data` with these properties:
66	
67	| Parameter | Description | Example |
68	|---|---|---|
69	| `countryISO` | Same as `session.custom.geCountry` | `GB` |
70	| `cultureCode` | Same as `session.custom.geCulture` | `en-GB` |
71	| `currencyCode` | Same as `session.custom.geCurrency` | `GBP` |
72	| `apiVersion` | Same as `session.custom.geApiVersion` | `2.1.4` |
73	
74	---
75	
76	## Custom hooks called during PWA checkout handoff
77	
78	These hooks fire server-side during the SendCart / order lifecycle.
79	The PWA does not call them directly, but their return values affect what Global-e receives.
80	
81	| Hook | When fired | Returns | Notes |
82	|---|---|---|---|
83	| `globale.getGuestEmail` | Before SendCart | Guest email string or `null` | Pre-populates shopper email in Global-e checkout |
84	| `globale.getCustomerAddresses` | Before SendCart | Array of addresses or `null` | Passes address book to Global-e for logged-in shopper |
85	| `globale.getCookieConsent` | Before SendCart | `0` (none) / `1` (all) / `2` (essential only) | Must reflect Didomi consent state |
86	| `globale.getAllowMailsFromMerchant` | Before SendCart | Boolean | Marketing opt-in state |
87	| `globale.getAllowDirectCommunicationFromMerchant` | Before SendCart | Boolean | Direct communication consent |
88	| `globale.beforeSendCartRequest` | Before SendCart | Void | Can mutate the SendCart payload; use with caution |
89	| `globale.validateCart` | On ValidateCart request | `{ errorCode, errorMessage, amendedProducts, reservationRequestId }` | Stock check; extend for third-party inventory |
90	| `globale.onAfterCreateOrder` | After SFCC order created | Void | Fires for both default and fallback order creation |
91	| `globale.onBeforePlaceOrder` | Before SFCC order placed | Void | OOTB updates cookie consent on order |
92	| `globale.onAfterPlaceOrder` | After SFCC order placed | Void | OOTB updates cookie consent on order |
93	
94	---
95	
96	## Pricing strategies
97	
98	Global-e supports three strategies, configured per SFCC price book via custom attributes.
99	
100	### Dynamic (converted pricing)
101	- Destination price is calculated from the SFCC base price + FX rate + coefficient + rounding rules.
102	- Price book flags: `geBasePricebook = true`, `geFixedPricebook = false`.
103	- `geApplicableToDynamicCountries` — comma-separated ISO2 country codes; empty = all dynamic countries.
104	
105	### Fixed (as-is final pricing)
106	- The SFCC price book value is shown directly to the shopper with no conversion.
107	- Price book flags: `geBasePricebook = false`, `geFixedPricebook = true`.
108	- `geApplicableToFixedCountries` — must be a non-empty CSV list; empty means fixed applicability is **false**.
109	- Price book `currencyCode` must match the fixed country's currency exactly.
110	
111	### Shared (one book for both)
112	- One price book acts as base for dynamic countries **and** as fixed for specific countries.
113	- Price book flags: both `geBasePricebook = true` and `geFixedPricebook = true`.
114	- Both scope CSV fields must be configured; currency rule for fixed countries still applies.
115	
116	**Promotion threshold note:**
117	- Dynamic countries: thresholds in the base merchant currency.
118	- Fixed countries: thresholds in the end-customer currency.
119	
120	---
121	
122	## Order number displayed to shoppers
123	
124	By default shoppers see the **Global-e order number** (format: `GE<digits><country>`, e.g. `GE111326998GB`) on:
125	- the order confirmation page,
126	- My Account / Order History,
127	- all transactional emails sent by Global-e.
128	
129	Domestic (SFCC-checkout) orders continue to show the SFCC order number.
130	
131	---
132	
133	## Order lifecycle — status transitions
134	
135	| Event | SFCC order status | Payment status | Export status |
136	|---|---|---|---|
137	| Order created (basket → order) | Created | Not Paid | Not Exported |
138	| SendOrderToMerchant received | **New** | Not Paid | Not Exported |
139	| PerformPayment received (fraud OK) | New | **Paid** | **Ready for Export** |
140	| Order cancelled (fraud fail / not confirmed) | **Cancelled** | Not Paid | — |
141	
142	---
143	
144	## Promotions — what works with Global-e checkout
145	
146	Supported promotion classes and discount types (Dynamic and Fixed pricing):
147	
148	- **Product promotions** — `PERCENTAGE`, `AMOUNT`, `FIXED_PRICE`, `PRICE_BOOK_PRICE`, `BONUS`, `BONUS_CHOICE` are all supported for both pricing strategies.
149	- **Order promotions** — `PERCENTAGE`, `AMOUNT`, `BONUS`, `BONUS_CHOICE` supported.
150	- **Shipping promotions** — only `FREE` shipping is supported; `PERCENTAGE`, `AMOUNT`, `FIXED_PRICE` on shipping are **not** supported.
151	- `TOTAL_FIXED_PRICE` (Buy X for Y total) — supported for both.
152	
153	Not supported for Global-e checkout:
154	- Fixed Price Shipping (`FIXED_PRICE` discount type on Shipping promotions)
155	- Free Shipping (`FREE` discount type on Product promotions — i.e. free-shipping-on-product-condition)
156	- `PERCENTAGE_OFF_OPTIONS` on product promotions with quantity qualifiers
157	
158	A promotion is only included in the Global-e handoff if it is valid, active, assigned to an ongoing Campaign, and triggered by a Customer Group, Coupon Code, or Source Code qualifier.
159	
160	---
161	
162	## Failover
163	
164	If Global-e services are unavailable, the integration can be disabled by setting the SFCC site preference **"Global-e Enabled"** to **"No"**. This is a manual SFCC-side action, not a PWA control.
165

1	# GiveX — Vendor Documentation (PWA-relevant extract)
2	
3	Source: GiveX integration kit. Contains only the portions directly relevant to PWA implementation (input validation, display, and TypeScript types). Protocol and transport details are MuleSoft's concern.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Card Number Format
8	
9	Two formats are in use:
10	
11	**IIN-prefixed:** `IIIIII RRRRR GGGGG C`
12	- `IIIIII` — ISO IIN (6-digit issuer identification number)
13	- `RRRRR` — Validation code / serial prefix
14	- `GGGGG` — Serial number
15	- `C` — Luhn check digit
16	
17	**Non-IIN:** `RRRRR GGGGG C`
18	
19	The **ISO-serial** representation is `{IIN}-{serial}`, e.g. `603628-258109479`. This is the form returned in balance-check responses.
20	
21	Relevant for: input field length/format validation; display masking.
22	
23	---
24	
25	## Security Code (PIN)
26	
27	The Security Code is an optional field in the GiveX protocol, but Zimmermann's merchant program has it enabled — the host validates the supplied code against the one assigned to the card. From the vendor FAQ:
28	
29	> "When making a purchase online and submitting payment by Givex redemption, the merchant may prompt the cardholder to enter the Security Code in addition to the Givex number, thus ensuring the identity of the cardholder."
30	
31	The Security Code must not be stored by the client system.
32	
33	Relevant for: PIN input field is mandatory UX (not optional) for Zimmermann's program.
34	
35	---
36	
37	## Balance Check Response Fields (API 994)
38	
39	These are the fields GiveX returns on a successful balance check. MuleSoft maps these before the PWA sees them, but this is the underlying shape:
40	
41	| Field | Type | Notes |
42	|---|---|---|
43	| Result | `"0"` on success, non-zero on error | Error text is for display only — may change without notice; use the result code for logic |
44	| Certificate balance | Decimal string, e.g. `"50.01"` | |
45	| Points balance | Decimal string | |
46	| Expiry date | `YYYY-MM-DD` string, or `"None"` if no expiry | |
47	| Currency code | ISO currency string, e.g. `"AUD"`, `"GBP"` | Currency of the card, not the storefront locale |
48	| ISO-serial | `{IIN}-{serial}` string, e.g. `"603628-258109479"` | The safe-to-display portion of the card number |
49	| Order type | `"0"` = Gift Card, `"1"` = Coupon | Determines label shown to customer |
50	
51	On error, GiveX returns a non-zero result code and a human-readable error message. The message text is not stable — program against the result code.
52

1	# MuleSoft — PWA Integration Reference
2	
3	*Source: MuleSoft technical design documents received from Tryzens (PDFs on file). PWA-relevant summary only — server-side flows are noted for boundary clarity but not detailed here.*
4	
5	MuleSoft (Anypoint Platform) is the integration middleware between SFCC, NewStore, AP21, Narvar, and Omneo. The vast majority of traffic is server-to-server and outside the PWA boundary. This document covers only the **PWA-direct path**: the confirmed endpoint contracts and response schemas for calls the Managed Runtime Node layer makes to MuleSoft.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. PWA-relevant APIs — confirmed
10	
11	### 1.1 Magento Experience API — orders, order detail, returns
12	
13	**API name (MuleSoft internal):** `magento-exp-api`  
14	**Source document:** *Magento Experience Integration v3.0 (18 Jun 2025)* + *Customer Order Transactions Sync Process API v2.0 (18 Jun 2025)*
15	
16	The PWA replaces the Magento storefront as the caller of this API. The Magento Experience API is the inbound tier; it calls the Order Transactions Sync Process API internally to fetch data from NewStore.
17	
18	#### Endpoints
19	
20	| Operation | Method | Path |
21	|---|---|---|
22	| Order history list | GET | `/api/orders?customer_id={customer_id}&offset={offset}&count={count}` |
23	| Order detail | GET | `/api/orders/{order_id}?id_type=internal` |
24	| Returns list | GET | `/api/returns?customer_id={customer_id}&offset={offset}&count={count}` |
25	
26	#### Base URLs
27	
28	| Environment | Base URL |
29	|---|---|
30	| Dev | `https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api-dev` |
31	| QA | `https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api-qa` |
32	| Prod | *(not yet provisioned)* |
33	
34	#### Authentication
35	
36	`client_id` and `client_secret` (MuleSoft platform credentials). These are **not** SLAS JWTs — MuleSoft does not verify shopper identity at the transport layer on this endpoint. The `customer_id` query parameter carries shopper identity; the contract for how the PWA proves that parameter is legitimate (impersonation prevention) is an open item — see §5.
37	
38	#### Retry strategy
39	
40	Maximum 3 attempts, 1-minute interval. MuleSoft sends a failure-notification email to admins after all retries are exhausted.
41	
42	#### Response time target
43	
44	`< 2.5 s` per MuleSoft non-functional requirements.

252	### 1.2 Find In Store — boutique stock availability
253	
254	**API name (MuleSoft internal):** `magento-exp-api` (same inbound tier as orders)  
255	**Source document:** *Find In Store Integration v1.0 (06 Feb 2025)*
256	
257	The PWA replaces Magento as the caller. The internal chain is: PWA → MuleSoft Magento Exp API → Product Availability Process API → NewStore System API.
258	
259	#### Endpoint
260	
261	| Operation | Method | Path |
262	|---|---|---|
263	| Boutique stock lookup | POST | `/api/find-in-store` |
264	
265	#### Base URLs
266	
267	| Environment | Base URL |
268	|---|---|
269	| Dev | `https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api-dev` |
270	| QA | `https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api-qa` |
271	| Prod | `https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api` |
272	
273	> Prod URL is provisioned for Find In Store (unlike the orders/returns endpoints where prod is still blank).
274	
275	#### Authentication
276	
277	`client_id` and `client_secret` passed as request credentials. These are MuleSoft platform credentials, not per-shopper identity. Find In Store does not require shopper authentication — it is a product+country lookup with no PII.
278	
279	#### Request
280	
281	```json
282	{
283	  "ProductId": "2000501",
284	  "CountryCode": "GB"
285	}
286	```
287	
288	`ProductId` is the NewStore `product_id` (a numeric string). `CountryCode` is an ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 code used to filter stores by region.
289	
290	#### Response
291	
292	```json
293	[
294	  { "StoreId": "31434", "qty": 1 },
295	  { "StoreId": "ZIMMERMANN_LONDON_STORE", "qty": 0 }
296	]
297	```
298	
299	`StoreId` may be a numeric string (`"31434"`) or a named NewStore location ID (`"ZIMMERMANN_LONDON_STORE"`). The PWA must handle both formats. `qty` is available-to-promise stock at that location.
300	
301	#### Retry strategy
302	
303	3 attempts, 600 ms delay between retries.

216	## 3. Product & Merchant Listing Schema — PDPs (DMU-037)
217	
218	Replaces the legacy flat `Product`-with-multiple-`Offer` shape (which Sparro flagged: `color` was an internal ID, brand was "Zimmermannwear", variant offers carried no `size` differentiator, missing merchant fields). The new shape uses a `ProductGroup` plus one `Product` node per size variant.

288	Field notes:
289	
290	- `color` is a **human-readable label** (e.g. "Deep Blue"), not an internal ID.
291	- `brand` is a nested `Brand` object literally `"ZIMMERMANN"` — not "Zimmermannwear".
292	- `productGroupID` uses the master SKU code.
293	- `variesBy` is currently `["size"]`. Add `"color"` if/when a single PDP renders multiple colourways.
294	- `hasMerchantReturnPolicy.merchantReturnDays` is **14 on `/uk/`** and **15 on all other storefronts** as of the Sparro deliverable. Must stay in sync with [returns.md §6](prd/returns.md) — CRM-066–068 is still TBC on whether the window is measured from delivery or shipment.
295	- Variant `Product`s carry their own `image` array, `gtin` (per-variant barcode), and a back-reference via `isVariantOf` to the `ProductGroup` `@id`.
296	- Availability and price drive off live SFCC inventory at SSR time (DMU-037).

415	## 4. Breadcrumb + CollectionPage + ItemList Schema — PLPs (DMU-038)
416	
417	To be implemented on every category page. One `@graph` block per page containing all three schema types, linked by `@id`.
418	
419	### 4.1 Template
420	
421	```json
422	{
423	  "@context": "https://schema.org",
424	  "@graph": [
425	    {
426	      "@type": "CollectionPage",
427	      "@id": "[Canonical URL of this category page]",
428	      "url": "[Canonical URL of this category page]",
429	      "name": "[Category Name]",
430	      "description": "[Meta description of this category]",
431	      "breadcrumb": {"@id": "[Canonical URL of this category page]#breadcrumb"},
432	      "mainEntity": {"@id": "[Canonical URL of this category page]#itemlist"}
433	    },
434	    {
435	      "@type": "BreadcrumbList",
436	      "@id": "[Canonical URL of this category page]#breadcrumb",
437	      "itemListElement": [
438	        {"@type": "ListItem", "position": 1, "name": "ZIMMERMANN", "item": "https://www.zimmermann.com/"},
439	        {"@type": "ListItem", "position": 2, "name": "[Parent Category Name]", "item": "[Parent Category URL]"},
440	        {"@type": "ListItem", "position": 3, "name": "[Current Category Name]", "item": "[Canonical URL of this category page]"}
441	        // Add more ListItems here if deeper in hierarchy, incrementing position number
442	      ]
443	    },
444	    {
445	      "@type": "ItemList",
446	      "@id": "[Canonical URL of this category page]#itemlist",
447	      "itemListOrder": "https://schema.org/ItemListOrderDescending",
448	      "numberOfItems": "[Total number of products on this page]",
449	      "itemListElement": [
450	        {"@type": "ListItem", "position": 1, "url": "[Product URL first]"},
451	        {"@type": "ListItem", "position": 2, "url": "[Product URL second]"},
452	        {"@type": "ListItem", "position": 3, "url": "[Product URL third]"}
453	        // LOOP: continue adding items for all products on the page
454	      ]
455	    }
456	  ]
457	}
458	```
459	
460	`ItemList` covers the **initial SSR'd product batch**, not the full category. Zimmermann PLPs use a "View more" pattern at 36 products per page — no paginated URLs ([plp.md §1.1](prd/plp.md)) — so the JSON-LD emitted server-side represents what the crawler sees on first paint, and there's no need to update it client-side as users load more. `numberOfItems` matches the count of `itemListElement` entries, not the full category size.

505	## 5. Decisions made adapting the Sparro templates to our PRD
506	
507	The Sparro workbook predates several of our finalised regional decisions (it was authored before the current `/en-eu/`, `/en-ca/`, `/en-ch/` URL structure was confirmed). The schema-org structure is unchanged from Sparro — these are template-level adaptations to match our PRD, not deviations from the SEO spec.
508	
509	1. **`/en-eu/` added to the per-site overrides table** as "ZIMMERMANN Europe". Sparro's checks sheet listed FR, IT, ES but omitted EN — assumed to be an oversight given EU domestic English is a real storefront ([regional.md §1](prd/regional.md)).
510	2. **`/en-ca/` and `/en-ch/` kept as standalone `WebSite` nodes**, naming as Sparro proposed ("ZIMMERMANN Canada" / "ZIMMERMANN Switzerland"). They are real URL prefixes with their own homepages even though they share inventory with their parent SFCC site, so a per-prefix `WebSite` is correct.
511	3. **Variant `gtin` omitted when null** (e.g. `0P` petite SKUs that carry no barcode). Do not emit `gtin: ""` or `gtin: null` — skip the field. Matches Sparro's example, which simply leaves `gtin` off the `0P` variant.
512	4. **`material` stays free-text** (e.g. `"Main: 100% polyester; lining: 100% cotton"`), sourced verbatim from the SFCC product attribute equivalent to Magento's current `material` field. A controlled vocabulary is a nice-to-have; not in launch scope.

A non-AU/non-Oceania human visitor landing on AU is redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; if no storefront matches their region, fall back to HK. Search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the redirect — match by User-Agent against a comprehensive allowlist (Googlebot incl. Image/News, Bingbot, DuckDuckBot, AppleBot, YandexBot, Baiduspider, Slackbot, Twitterbot, facebookexternalhit, LinkedInBot, WhatsApp, Discordbot). Fail open: if UA looks botty but isn't matched, skip the redirect rather than apply it — false-positive cost is zero, missing a real crawler hurts SEO.

7	## 1. Tag Management & Data Layer (AAB-001, AAB-002)
8	
9	- **GTM container** must load on every page across all regional storefronts (AAB-001). The container snippet loads via the **Addingwell MRT integration** (per Third_Party_Integrations "Google Tag Manager" row). All tag firing rules and GTM *container logic* are owned by Zimmermann/Tell No Lies inside GTM — Accenture's responsibility ends at loading the snippet and correctly emitting the data layer from SFCC.
10	- **Mechanism note:** AAB-001's signed-off Zimmermann comment ("we will manage everything in the GTM container, not in Addingwell") refers to where *container/tag logic* lives — it does **not** mean Addingwell is absent from the stack. Addingwell operates as a **server-side container** routing analytics events (Third_Party_Integrations "Adding Well" row), and is the MRT integration through which the GTM snippet itself loads. Addingwell container configuration and tag routing remain out of SFCC scope (owned by Zimmermann/Tell No Lies).
11	- **Data layer** must be native to SFCC and serve as the single source of truth for all downstream analytics and marketing tags. It must cover, but is not limited to (AAB-002):
12	  - Standard ecommerce events across the full shopping journey: product viewed, product impressions, add to cart, cart viewed, checkout initiated, shipping info entered, payment info entered, order confirmed.
13	  - A complete product data schema per event: SKU, name, price, category, quantity, stock status, list position.
14	  - Local currency mapped per active regional storefront.
15	  - Customer identifiers to support cross-platform linking across analytics, CRM, and loyalty.
16	  - Attributes required for advertising platform pixel firing (Meta, Pinterest, TikTok, Google Ads, Bing Ads, LinkedIn): event type, transaction data, product data, hashed customer identifiers.
17	  - Customer attributes on every relevant event: hashed email (SHA-256), login state, existing customer flag, lifetime value, customer type, loyalty status, customer group, current store view.
18	  - Customer region on every event, sourced from both Zimmermann's geolocation logic and the Global-e platform.
19	- Tell No Lies owns the Data Dictionary; the GTM container consumes the data layer and routes to downstream tools. All *container/tag logic* is managed within the GTM container, not configured in Addingwell (AAB-001, amended scope 2026-05-05) — though events are routed server-side through the Addingwell container downstream (Third_Party_Integrations "Google Analytics 4" + "Adding Well" rows). Downstream, core commerce/analytics events are handled by Sparro and Addingwell (AAB-003).

21	> **Flag — residual tension to reconcile.** AAB-001 (Analytics sheet) frames everything as living "in the GTM container, not in addingwell", while the Third_Party_Integrations GTM, GA4 and Addingwell rows describe the GTM snippet loading *via the Addingwell MRT integration* and events routing through an *Addingwell server-side container*. These reconcile if "not in addingwell" is read as *tag/container configuration*, not the loading/routing transport — but the two sheets use Addingwell inconsistently. Confirm with Tell No Lies which Addingwell role (none / transport-only / server-side routing) is correct before build. This is a documentation flag, not a resolved position.

26	- GTM container config, tag firing rules, Addingwell container configuration, and GA4 setup are all owned by Tell No Lies and are **out of SFCC scope**. **Exception (per AAB-004/AAB-005, confirmed 09-06-2026):** Optimizely and Crazy Egg are **not** in the GTM container — the PWA loads each as a **separate front-end tag in the page head** (see §3–§4). 151	## 10. Security & Handling of Card Numbers
152	
153	Gift card numbers and PINs are treated as payment credentials (per *GIVEX Numbers Defined.pdf*: a GiveX card is `[prefix][serial][check]`, only the **serial portion** may be displayed or logged). For PWA work this means:
154	
155	- **Transport.** Card number and PIN must be sent in the request **body** (POST), never as a query string. URLs end up in MRT access logs, browser history, and Referer headers.
156	- **Storage.** No `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, or cookie may hold the full card number or PIN. Form state lives in React only and is cleared on unmount.
157	- **Logging.** No `console.log`, no Sentry breadcrumb / `beforeSend` capture, no GTM dataLayer push, no analytics event may contain the full card number or PIN. Add a redaction filter in the logger and a Sentry scrubber for the gift-card payload. Do not enable body-logging middleware on the MRT balance-check route.
158	- **Display.** After submission, render only the serial portion (e.g. `••••••••1234`). The applied-gift-cards list in cart/checkout stores the masked form returned by SFCC — never echo back the original input.
159	- **Server-side.** MRT forwards the payload to MuleSoft — which owns the GiveX socket for both balance check (MRT → MuleSoft → GiveX) and redemption (NewStore adaptor → MuleSoft → GiveX) — and returns only the masked response to the browser, see §11. The full PAN does not appear in any MRT log, response body, or persisted store. The unmasked-PAN boundary sits with MuleSoft/GiveX, not the PWA.
160	
161	(Cross-reference: [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../.claude/rules/conventions.md) — Logging.)
162	
163	---
164	
165	## 11. Architecture Note — PWA ↔ GiveX
166	
167	Two distinct integration paths. The Third-Party Integrations row describes balance check as a *"direct MRT API connection"* and redemption as *"via the NewStore adaptor through MuleSoft"*. Confirmed with Integration: *"direct MRT"* means **MRT-initiated** (not via SFCC) — **MuleSoft remains the upstream for balance check**, because GiveX is reachable only over a persistent socket the MRT runtime cannot hold.
168	
169	- **Balance check (My Account, GC-051–062; Check Balance link, GC-037).** PWA → MRT → **MuleSoft** → GiveX. GiveX exposes only a persistent TCP socket (JSON-RPC/XML-RPC) that the MRT Workers runtime cannot hold, so MuleSoft owns the GiveX socket pool, primary/secondary host failover, and credentials. MRT exposes an HTTPS endpoint, applies rate-limit / bot protection in front of the unauthenticated balance-check route (see §9, GC-062), and holds the MuleSoft credential as an env var.
170	- **Checkout redemption (GC-034–049).** Gift card and credit note redemption is handled **via the NewStore adaptor through MuleSoft**. Real-time validation on Apply (GC-039) and the resulting payment-instrument state (masked number, applied amount, remaining balance) flow back to the PWA through that path. The PWA does not hold any GiveX socket itself.
171	- **Reversal on capture failure.** If GiveX redemption succeeds but downstream card capture (Adyen) fails, reversal/cancel is handled by the redemption path (NewStore adaptor → MuleSoft → GiveX), not the PWA.
172	
173	PWA-side blockers before live wiring is possible:
174	- GiveX balance-check API contract for the MuleSoft connection (request/response schema, error taxonomy mapping to GC-042 / GC-060 / GC-061).
175	- GiveX endpoint URLs and credential per environment (dev / UAT / prod).
176	- Redemption payload/response shape exposed through the NewStore adaptor / MuleSoft for cart/checkout.
177	
178	Until those are published, balance-check work proceeds against a typed mock; checkout redemption work waits on the redemption contract.
179

26	- AU and EU sites display prices **inclusive of tax** (GST/VAT included). Same base price across all EU countries — differing VAT rates handled in the background (PRC-05, confirmed — signed off by Dani + Emma)
27	- US site displays prices **exclusive of tax**; Avalara calculates per-state tax added at checkout (PRC-06, confirmed — signed off by Dani + Emma)
28	- Bulk assignment of tax class to products supported — tax class driven by AP21 taxonomy ID (derived from product category, configured by finance) fed into SFCC via MuleSoft; no manual bulk updates required. Avalara covers AU, EU, US, and UK domestic storefronts for go-live. International storefronts (HK, ME, US Int'l, EU Int'l) handled through Global-e. HS code handling may still need further exploration but is not a go-live blocker (PRC-07, confirmed — signed off by Emma/Rebecca 2026-06-24)
29	- Product prices displayed consistently in storefront currency across PLP, PDP, mini-bag, cart, wishlist, recommended tiles, and checkout (PRC-08, PRC-33)
30	
31	---
32	
33	## 3. Sale & Markdown Pricing (PRC-09 – PRC-13)
34	
35	- Original list price displayed alongside active sale price — shown on PLP tiles, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, wishlist, recommended tiles, and order history. Note (DR): sale items are usually excluded from recommendations via a manual rule (PRC-09)
36	- Business users can schedule sale pricing to go live at a specified future date and time. Category pre-merchandised; team QCs via live-preview before go-live (PRC-10, confirmed)
37	- **SFCC native storefront preview** supports QC of scheduled pricing and category changes before go-live, including preview for specific customer groups — scoped to SFCC OOTB preview, no custom build (PRC-11, confirmed)
38	- Final sale flag supported on products (PRC-12, confirmed). Assumption: `is_returnable` drives returnable status, `final_sale` drives front-end final-sale messaging. Attribute distinction and AP21 derivation still to be confirmed — see Open Items. No final-sale icon in design yet
39	- Price display behaviour based on AP21 `MarkdownStatus` values (permanent / temporary / temppermanent) — open: Zimmermann to confirm what each value means and what storefront behaviour it should drive (PRC-13, open)
40	
41	---
42	
43	## 4. Multi-Currency & Regional Pricebooks (PRC-14, PRC-36 – PRC-43, PRC-47 – PRC-52)
44	
45	- Country/currency selector shows prices in the currency configured for the customer's selected shipping country (PRC-14, confirmed). Note (RJ): the country selector is not present on the AU site
46	- **Country-to-currency mapping** configurable in SFCC Business Manager without code deployment (PRC-36, PRC-52)
47	- Per currency, the system stores the **conversion approach**: (a) Base RRP, (b) Fixed Pricelist from AP21, (c) Fixed FX rate from base, or (d) Dynamic FX rate from base (PRC-37)
48	- **Nightly job** loads Global-e pricing into SFCC: FX rates, price coefficients, and rounding rules (PRC-38)
49	- Pricebooks generated from Global-e pricing data and imported into SFCC (PRC-39)
50	- Target-currency price calculation: `base pricebook price × FX rate × country coefficient × product-class coefficient` (PRC-40)
51	- Calculated prices included in the SFCC search index for price-based filters and sort on PLP/search (PRC-41)
52	- All promotion calculations executed in the customer's selected ship-to currency (PRC-42)
53	- **Currency display formatting** per locale: symbol position, decimal places (including zero-decimal currencies), thousand separator, minus-sign for refunds (PRC-47)
54	- **FX rate locked at order placement** and applied to any refund at the same locked rate — refund in target currency equals original charged amount (PRC-48)
55	- **Currency rounding strategy** per currency (e.g. nearest whole AED, 2 decimal EUR, 0 decimal JPY); applied at line-item level before tax/promotion stacking (PRC-49)
56	- Business Manager interface for authorised users: view conversion approach per currency, set/change conversion approach, view current FX rate with last-updated timestamp and feed status; read-only access for merchandising team (PRC-50)
57	- Bulk import/export of currency config via SFCC Site Import/Export, OCAPI, or deployment scripts — technical users only (PRC-51)
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 5. VIC & Customer Group Pricing (PRC-17 – PRC-19)
62	
63	Customer-group-specific catalogue pricing — visible on PLP, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, recommended tiles, wishlist (not cart-only discounts). Discounts do not apply to products already on sale or to gift cards.
64	
65	| Customer group | Discount |
66	|---|---|
67	| Gold VIC | Permanent 10% off all non-sale products |
68	| Platinum VIC | Permanent discount — rate TBC (Zimmermann to confirm) |
69	| VIC early access | Flat 30% off before public sale goes live; removed before public sale |
70	| Advent customers | e.g. 50% off during Advent events |
71	| PR companies and investors | Configured discount |
72	
73	- **Customer group discounts do NOT stack on sale items** (PRC-18, revised per DR): sale items are excluded from promotion set-ups. Example: a Gold VIC customer receives 10% off full-price items, but if they add a sale product to cart they get the sale price only — no extra 10% on top. The system must continue to support this exclusion.
74	- Configurable priority rules in SFCC Business Manager (e.g. Gold VIC 10% excludes gift cards and items already on sale) (PRC-19)
75	
76	---
77	
78	## 6. Global-e Pricing & Cart Handoff (PRC-15 – PRC-16, PRC-43 – PRC-46, PRC-53 – PRC-55)
79	
80	- DDP/DDU duties messaging on PDP per country — configurable per country (PRC-15)
81	- SFCC passes a **complete cart to Global-e** in the customer's target currency at international checkout, including: all line items with quantities, prices in target currency, all applied promotions and coupon codes, Retail Rewards, gift cards, and a placeholder/dummy shipping method. Global-e adds actual shipping charges and processes payment (PRC-16, PRC-43). Note (DR): current M2 implementation has limitations — Global-e does not accept M2 catalogue promotions where the discount price appears on PLP/PDP for logged-in customer groups. Open (25.05): confirm with Global-e whether the SFCC cartridge supports honouring customer-group catalogue prices at Global-e checkout; if not currently honoured in M2, Zimmermann to confirm how these VIC/customer-group customers are receiving their discounts at international checkout today (e.g. configured directly in Global-e).
82	- **Coupon codes**: validation occurs in SFCC; discount values passed to Global-e in cart payload — Global-e does not call back to SFCC to re-validate (PRC-46, open — workbook shows Confirmed 2026-06-24, but sign-off comment conditions delivery on Global-e being able to apply and validate coupons: "This will be delivered only if Global-e can support." Treated as open until Global-e confirms capability; see Open Items)
83	- **Gift card webhooks**: GiveX gift card validate/redeem/refund webhooks exposed to Global-e (PRC-44)
84	- **Retail Rewards at Global-e checkout**: applied after promotions (PRC-45, open — RJ challenges the "max 1 reward per order" limit: "Multiple retail rewards can be applied per order". Max-rewards-per-order count to be confirmed; see Open Items)
85	- Customers can purchase GiveX gift cards as products at Global-e checkout; provisioned in GiveX via existing middleware after payment (PRC-53, confirmed). Note (RJ): for Global-e regions gift cards are digital-only; currency coverage to be confirmed — see Open Items
86	- **Daily Global-e catalogue export job**: generates and uploads a product catalogue CSV to Global-e via SFTP for product-level restrictions, VAT rates, and HS code assignments (PRC-54)
87	- Authentication configured between SFCC and Global-e for all API calls (PRC-55)
88	
89	---
90	
91	## 7. Open Items
92	
93	- RetailPrice functional confirmation owner outstanding (EK query) — assumption is RetailPrice stored as an additional SFCC price field (PRC-01)
94	- Final sale vs. is_returnable attribute distinction and AP21 derivation — Zimmermann to confirm; no final-sale icon in design yet (PRC-12, otherwise confirmed)
95	- AP21 MarkdownStatus values (permanent / temporary / temppermanent) and storefront behaviour — Zimmermann to confirm (PRC-13)
96	- Platinum VIC permanent discount rate — TBC (PRC-17)
97	- Fixed pricelists once imported via MuleSoft — CS query: confirm in-system accessibility vs. today's SFTP append (PRC-35, otherwise confirmed)
98	- **Coupon codes at Global-e checkout** — workbook shows Confirmed 2026-06-24, but sign-off comment is conditional: "RJ / Mani need to confirm that the coupon can be applied and is validated through Global-e. This will be delivered only if Global-e can support." Confirm with Global-e that the SFCC cartridge can apply and validate coupon codes before this requirement is treated as confirmed (PRC-46)
99	- Global-e SFCC cartridge support for customer-group catalogue prices at international checkout (PRC-43) — confirm with Global-e; Zimmermann to confirm current M2 workaround for VIC pricing at Global-e checkout
100	- Retail Rewards count at Global-e checkout — requirement states max 1 reward per order; RJ challenges: "Multiple retail rewards can be applied per order". Confirm max-per-order before implementing (PRC-45)
101	- GiveX gift cards at Global-e checkout — digital-only for Global-e regions (RJ); confirm whether offered in all supported currencies (PRC-53, otherwise confirmed)

1	# 17 — Measmerize (Find My Size / Size Guide)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Measmerize is the third-party sizing widget on the PDP. It powers two surfaces:
6	
7	1. **Find My Size** — takes body measurements from the customer, generates a size recommendation, and updates the CTA to display "Recommended: Size X" (PRD-050).
8	2. **Size guide overlay** — opens as a slide-out without navigating away from the PDP (PRD-053, confirmed — size guide is a Measmerize overlay).
9	
10	The PWA's job is narrow: inject the Measmerize script on PDP, place the required DOM containers, detect whether Measmerize has data for the current product, and fall back to the Contentful-managed size guide if it does not.
11	
12	In scope:
13	
14	- Script injection on PDP (once on first mount, deferred behind LCP)
15	- Placing DOM containers (`#measmerize-modal`, `#measmerize-recommendation`)
16	- Detecting data availability via custom events and showing or hiding the trigger accordingly
17	- Updating the product code via the Global Object on SPA navigation
18	- Rendering the Contentful size guide as a fallback when Measmerize has no data for the product
19	- Injecting the checkout tracking script on the order confirmation page
20	
21	Out of scope:
22	
23	- Widget configuration in the Measmerize console (Zimmermann and Measmerize own this)
24	- Size guide content — Measmerize owns it where the widget has data; Contentful owns the fallback
25	- Measurement units toggle (cm / inches) — part of the Contentful fallback size guide (PRD-056), not the Measmerize widget
26	
27	## 2. How it works
28	
29	```
30	PDP page mounts
31	        │
32	        ▼
33	PWA injects Measmerize script tag once (deferred — after LCP image)
34	  with data-brand-code, data-product-code (SFCC SKU), data-lang-code, data-country-code
35	        │
36	        ▼
37	Measmerize initialises and checks its data store for this product
38	        │
39	        ├── data exists → fires measmerize.widget.ready
40	        │       │
41	        │       ▼
42	        │   Measmerize mounts the widget in #measmerize-modal
43	        │   Customer clicks → Measmerize takes over and renders its overlay
44	        │   Recommendation generated → fires measmerize.widget.recommend
45	        │   PWA reads event.detail.defaultSize to show "Recommended: Size X"
46	        │
47	        └── no data → fires measmerize.widget.unavailable
48	                PWA shows the Contentful size guide link instead
49	                Customer clicks → PWA renders its own slide-out
50	                                  with Contentful content + cm/in toggle
51	```
52	
53	**Integration modes:** Measmerize supports two DOM integration patterns:
54	
55	- **Standard** — place `<div id="measmerize-button">` on the PDP. Measmerize renders and manages its own "Find Your Size" button inside it. Use when no pre-existing size-guide modal exists.
56	- **Modal** — the PWA provides its own CTAs (e.g. separate "Find My Size" and "Size Guide" links). When the customer opens the overlay, the PWA calls `window.measmerize.modal.mount()`, which injects the widget into `<div id="measmerize-modal">`. No `#measmerize-button` div is needed.
57	
58	Both surfaces (Find My Size and Size Guide) point to the same Measmerize widget.
59	
60	**Confirmed 2026-07-06: Modal Integration is the required path.** The PWA owns the modal/slide-out shell (width, styling, tab switching between the Measmerize widget and the Contentful size guide fallback); Measmerize is inserted into it via `window.measmerize.modal.mount()`, which injects Measmerize's HTML directly into `<div id="measmerize-modal">` (not an iframe). The `#measmerize-button` div is not used.
61	
62	**Injection pattern:** Inject the script once on first PDP mount inside a `useEffect` with an empty dependency array. Never place it inside a dynamically re-rendered container.
63	
64	**SPA navigation:** When the customer navigates to a different product (no page reload), update the product code via the Global Object:
65	
66	```js
67	window.measmerize.script.productCode = 'NEW_SKU';
68	```
69	
70	`brandCode` cannot be changed at runtime — it requires a page reload.
71	
72	**Modal re-mount:** If React re-renders the `#measmerize-modal` container, call `window.measmerize.modal.mount()` to restore the widget.
73	
74	**SSR pre-check (optional):** To avoid a flash of the wrong UI on first paint, an unauthenticated REST check can determine at SSR time whether Measmerize has data for a product:
75	
76	```
77	GET https://api.client.measmerize.com/integrations/v1/brands/{brandCode}/products/{productCode}
78	```
79	
80	Returns `200` if Measmerize has the product, `404` if not.
81	
82	**Cleanup:** Remove event listeners and the script element on full component unmount.
83	
84	### Key custom events
85	
86	Events are fired on the script element (`document.getElementById('measmerize-script')`):
87	
88	| Event                           | When it fires                                                  | Payload                                                  |
89	| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
90	| `measmerize.script.ready`       | Script loaded with a valid brand code                          | —                                                        |
91	| `measmerize.script.unavailable` | Script loaded with an invalid brand code                       | —                                                        |
92	| `measmerize.widget.ready`       | Widget has data for this product and is about to mount         | —                                                        |
93	| `measmerize.widget.unavailable` | Widget has no data for this product — show Contentful fallback | —                                                        |
94	| `measmerize.widget.recommend`   | A recommendation was generated                                 | `event.detail.defaultSize`, `event.detail.convertedSize` |
95	| `measmerize.widget.addToCart`   | Customer clicked Add to Cart inside the widget                 | `event.detail.size`                                      |
96	
97	## 3. Credentials and script attributes
98	
99	| Credential / attribute         | Value                                                                          | Sensitivity   |
100	| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------- |
101	| Script URL                     | `https://client.measmerize.com/script.js`                                      | Public        |
102	| Checkout script URL            | `https://client.measmerize.com/checkout.js`                                    | Public        |
103	| `data-brand-code` (staging)    | `b38fac52-7328-45c9-9fd8-038fac4be58e` — shared across Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage | Public        |
104	| `data-brand-code` (production) | `131b0b3c-1578-4fb0-a7b9-c46cd634843d`                                         | Public        |
105	| `data-product-code`            | SFCC product SKU                                                               | Not sensitive |
106	| `data-lang-code`               | ISO 639-1 language code (e.g. `en`, `fr`) — from storefront locale             | Not sensitive |
107	| `data-country-code`            | ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 (e.g. `AU`, `GB`) — from storefront context                 | Not sensitive |
108	
109	The script tag uses `id="measmerize-script"` and the `async` attribute. No server-side call or MRT proxy is needed; the script is CDN-served and the brand code is a public identifier. All eight storefronts use the widget — `data-lang-code` and `data-country-code` must be set from the storefront context on every PDP.
110	
111	**Checkout tracking script:** Inject `checkout.js` on the order confirmation page only, with `data-brand-code` and `data-order-code` (the SFCC order ID). This enables ML training and return-rate reporting for Measmerize. It is independent of the PDP widget script.
112	
113	**CSP domains:** Measmerize serves a brand-specific CSS bundle and JS assets from `static.client.measmerize.com` (seeing the Moncler website as their example). Both `style-src` and `script-src` in `overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts` must include this origin.
114	
115	## 4. Consent and gating
116	
117	Measmerize sets cookies in three categories:
118	
119	- **Essential** — session and recommendation matching. Cannot be disabled; always set when the script loads.
120	- **Functional / Personalisation** — stored body measurements across PDPs. Disable via `window.measmerize.cookies.disableFunctional()`.
121	- **Analytical** — Google Analytics and Measmerize custom tracking. Disable via `window.measmerize.tracking.disableAnalytics()` and `window.measmerize.tracking.disableCustom()`.
122	
123	The consent approach is an open item (§5.1): whether to load the script freely and disable non-essential tracking via the SDK when consent is denied, or to gate the entire script load behind a Didomi consent category. The implementation must be built so the gate can be switched without changing the injection logic.
124	
125	## 5. Performance
126	
127	The Measmerize script is injected after the LCP image has painted — it is never on the critical paint path. If consent-gated, it loads only after Didomi consent, pushing the load further off the critical path. The Contentful fallback size guide loads lazily as part of the slide-out component.
128	
129	## 6. Failure modes and graceful degradation
130	
131	| Failure                                                            | Behaviour                                                                                         |
132	| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
133	| Script fails to load (CDN outage, network block, consent declined) | Fall back silently to the Contentful size guide.                                                  |
134	| Script loads but signals no data (`measmerize.widget.unavailable`) | Show the Contentful size guide link. This is the expected path for some products.                 |
135	| Contentful size guide also unavailable                             | Hide the size guide entry point entirely. Do not show a broken overlay.                           |
136	| Measmerize overlay fails to open after customer click              | Show a toast: "Size guide temporarily unavailable." The purchase flow is never blocked on sizing. |
137	
138	## 7. Open items requiring client confirmation
139	
140	1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm which of two approaches applies: (a) load the script freely and call `window.measmerize.tracking.disableAnalytics()` / `disableCustom()` / `cookies.disableFunctional()` when consent is denied (Essential cookies always run), or (b) gate the entire script load behind a Didomi consent category. This is a **blocking** decision. If approach (b) is chosen, Zimmermann Privacy to also confirm the Didomi consent category and Tell No Lies to supply the corresponding Didomi vendor / feature ID. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

1	# 18 — Vimeo (Product and Editorial Video)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Vimeo hosts video content embedded in the Zimmermann storefront at two surfaces:
6	
7	1. **Product video on PDP** — runway and campaign clips in the product gallery (PRD-066, PRD-067).
8	2. **Editorial video on content pages** — brand and campaign video referenced via embed URL in Contentful CMS entries (HPC-003, HPC-004).
9	
10	**Vimeo as the video platform is not yet confirmed (PRD-067 open).** This doc is provisional until that decision is made — see open item §6.1.
11	
12	The PWA's job is to embed the Vimeo player as a facade-loaded iframe and apply the correct privacy posture per the confirmed consent approach (§4). All other concerns — video hosting, transcoding, CDN delivery, player configuration — are owned by Vimeo and Zimmermann.
13	
14	In scope:
15	- Facade-loaded Vimeo iframe embed on PDP and editorial/content pages
16	- Applying `dnt=1` or Didomi consent gating per the confirmed approach (§4)
17	- Adding `player.vimeo.com` to the `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` directive
18	- Graceful fallback when Vimeo is unavailable or an embed URL is missing
19	
20	Out of scope:
21	- Video upload, hosting, and management in Vimeo (Zimmermann)
22	- Player configuration (colours, controls, autoplay) — set via embed URL parameters or Vimeo account settings
23	
24	## 2. How it works
25	
26	```
27	Page renders
28	        │
29	        ▼
30	PWA renders a lightweight facade:
31	  • poster image (lazy-loaded, correct aspect ratio)
32	  • play button overlay
33	  • no Vimeo JS loaded yet
34	        │
35	        ▼
36	Customer clicks play (or video scrolls into view for muted autoplay hero clips)
37	        │
38	        ▼
39	PWA swaps facade for the Vimeo iframe embed URL
40	  (with ?dnt=1, or standard URL gated behind consent, per confirmed approach — §4)
41	        │
42	        ▼
43	Vimeo player loads and begins playback
44	```
45	
46	**PDP:** the embed URL is stored in product data (sourced from Contentful or SFCC product attributes — content ownership is a Contentful open item, openItems §2.2).
47	
48	**Editorial pages:** the CMS author pastes the Vimeo share URL into a Contentful field. The PWA reads and embeds it.
49	
50	No authentication or credentials are required. The embed URL is a public Vimeo player URL — no server-side call or MRT proxy is needed.
51	
52	## 3. Performance
53	
54	- The facade keeps the Vimeo player JS entirely off the critical path. The player loads only on click or on scroll-into-view (muted autoplay hero clips only).
55	- The poster image is lazy-loaded and served at the correct display size from the Contentful Images API or the Vimeo thumbnail API. Never serve full-resolution frames at thumbnail dimensions.
56	- If consent approach (b) is chosen and consent has not been granted, the facade stays visible — no additional performance impact from a deferred load.
57	
58	## 4. Consent and gating
59	
60	Vimeo's standard embed sets analytics and tracking cookies unless the `dnt=1` query parameter is appended (`https://player.vimeo.com/video/{id}?dnt=1`). With `dnt=1`, Vimeo suppresses all tracking cookies and no Didomi gate is needed.
61	
62	Two possible approaches:
63	
64	- **(a) Always use `dnt=1`** — no consent gate required. The facade swaps in the `?dnt=1` URL unconditionally. Simpler implementation.
65	- **(b) Standard embed gated behind Didomi consent** — without consent the facade stays visible. With consent, the standard embed URL loads. Tell No Lies to supply the Didomi vendor / feature ID.
66	
67	**This is a blocking open item (§6.1).** The implementation supports either path without structural change; only the embed URL construction and the optional consent-gate wrapper differ.
68	
69	Fail closed: if consent state cannot be determined and approach (b) is chosen, the facade stays — no Vimeo iframe loads.
70	
71	## 5. Failure modes and graceful degradation
72	
73	| Failure | Behaviour |
74	|---|---|
75	| Vimeo CDN unavailable or iframe fails to load | Facade poster image stays visible. Do not show an error; do not break the page layout. |
76	| Embed URL missing from product data or CMS entry | Omit the video from the PDP gallery or the video section from the editorial page. No broken placeholder. |
77	| Consent approach (b): customer declines consent | Facade stays visible with no play affordance, or a brief inline "Enable analytics cookies to watch" message — design decision. Never block the surrounding page. |
78	
79	## 6. Open items requiring client confirmation
80	
81	1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm: (a) always append `dnt=1` to the embed URL — no Didomi gate needed; or (b) load the standard embed gated behind a Didomi consent category — Tell No Lies to supply the Didomi vendor / feature ID. This is a **blocking** decision. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
82	
83	2. **Vimeo platform confirmation (PRD-067).** The Third Party Integrations sheet lists Vimeo as the video platform, but PRD-067 is explicitly open: "Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed — open action to confirm best solution for smoothest FE experience." Zimmermann to confirm Vimeo as the platform before PDP video implementation begins. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

1	# 12 — Didomi (Consent Management Platform)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Didomi is the Consent Management Platform (CMP) for all seven Zimmermann storefronts. It is the gatekeeper for every third-party script that loads in the browser — marketing tags, analytics tags, heatmap and session-replay tools, the live-chat widget, the Adyen Drop-in, the Narvar EDD widget, and Google reCAPTCHA all wait on a Didomi signal before initialising.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- First-load cookie banner and consent UI
10	- Persistence of consent choices across sessions and pages
11	- Re-prompt and preference-centre access
12	- Consent callbacks consumed by application code to gate downstream scripts
13	- Google Consent Mode v2 signal emission (`ad_storage`, `ad_user_data`, `ad_personalization`, `analytics_storage`)
14	
15	Out of scope of this document:
16	
17	- The downstream tags themselves — owned by Tell No Lies inside the GTM container
18	- Server-side consent recording or back-office reporting
19	
20	## 2. Browser-side architecture
21	
22	```
23	First page load
24	        │
25	        ▼
26	@didomi/react component mounted at the top of the React tree
27	   (which injects Didomi loader from sdk.privacy-center.org)
28	        │
29	        ▼
30	Didomi SDK initialises ─────► reads persisted consent (cookie + localStorage)
31	        │
32	        ├── consent already given → fires consent.changed immediately
33	        │           │
34	        │           ▼
35	        │     App listeners load gated scripts (GTM, Inside Chat,
36	        │     Narvar EDD widget, Adyen, reCAPTCHA, etc.)
37	        │
38	        └── no prior consent → Didomi renders the banner
39	                    │
40	                    ▼
41	                User makes a choice
42	                    │
43	                    ▼
44	                consent.changed event fires with the new purpose and vendor IDs
45	```
46	
47	- The PWA uses the **`@didomi/react`** package to mount the SDK as early as possible at the top of the React tree. This is the Didomi-recommended approach for SPAs and keeps configuration tied to a single component rather than a raw script tag.
48	- The SDK's loader is fetched asynchronously from `sdk.privacy-center.org`. Configuration (notice copy, purposes, vendors) is pulled from the Didomi Console at runtime — the loader URL itself is environment-agnostic; the per-environment Notice ID identifies the configuration.
49	- The PWA registers listeners for `consent.changed` and per-vendor status changes. Each gated integration subscribes to the specific purpose or vendor ID it requires; on grant, it dynamically imports or injects its script tag.
50	- SSR HTML must not contain markup whose presence or content depends on consent state — consent-driven UI is hydrated on the client. This keeps the SSR cache consent-agnostic and avoids cumulative layout shift.
51	- No consent rules are hard-coded in the storefront. All configuration (notice copy, purposes, vendors) is owned by the Privacy team in the Didomi Console.
52	
53	## 3. Credentials
54	
55	- **Public credential:** the Didomi Notice ID, embedded in the `@didomi/react` component props. Safe to ship in the browser bundle.
56	- **No machine credential is required from the storefront** — the SDK authenticates using the Notice ID alone.
57	- **Per-environment Notice IDs:** separate Didomi Notices are provisioned per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod) so non-production traffic never affects production consent reporting. The PWA reads the active Notice ID from an environment variable resolved at build / runtime.
58	
59	## 4. Data exchanged
60	
61	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
62	|---|---|---|
63	| Browser → Didomi | None at runtime — consent UI is rendered by the SDK from the Console configuration | n/a |
64	| Didomi → Browser | Consent state: per-purpose booleans, per-vendor booleans, IAB TCF string, regulation applied, opaque user ID | `consent.changed` event and `Didomi.getCurrentUserStatus()` |
65	| Browser → GTM dataLayer | Default and updated Consent Mode v2 signals | `gtag('consent', 'default' \| 'update', …)` |
66	
67	The storefront does not pass PII to Didomi. The Didomi user ID is an opaque consent identifier — it is not joined to the SFCC customer profile and is never written to the customer record.
68	
69	## 5. Consent and gating contract
70	
71	Every PWA-direct integration that loads a third-party script subscribes to one of the buckets below. The storefront's configurable consent categories are **Performance, Analytics, and Marketing**, with **Required** always granted (REG-051). The exact Didomi purpose IDs used in production are owned by the Privacy team in the Console; the table is the application-side mapping.
72	
73	| Bucket | Purpose family | Scripts gated |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| Required (strictly necessary) | Always granted, no banner consent | Didomi itself; SFCC SCAPI; Contentful Delivery API; PWA→MRT proxy reads; Adyen Drop-in — **not Didomi consent-gated**: payment is strictly necessary and the Drop-in loads at the payment step regardless of consent state. The fail-closed rule (§8) applies to analytics/marketing scripts, not payment. |
76	| Analytics / measurement | `analytics`, `measure_content_performance` | GTM analytics tags (GA4 and anything Tell No Lies routes to it); Crazy Egg (all storefronts — AAB-005) and Optimizely Web (US storefront only — AAB-004) — both frontend-direct scripts, not in GTM. **Consent categories are TBC — Zimmermann to confirm** |
77	| Marketing / advertising | `create_ads_profile`, `select_personalized_ads`, `targeted_advertising` | Meta Pixel, GTM marketing tags, Enhanced Conversions |
78	| Performance | `improve_products`, `personalize_content` | Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) EDD **(TBC)**, Google Maps address autocomplete, Inside Chat **(TBC — consent category to be confirmed with Tell No Lies)**, Omneo widget (vendor disclosure only) |
79	| reCAPTCHA | **EU & UK: consent-gated (TBC)** — loads only post-consent in those regions; no consent required on other storefronts at form interaction | Google reCAPTCHA site-key load on the relevant forms |
80	
81	Adyen is a payment necessity and defers load until the customer reaches checkout, so it does not contribute to LCP on any other page. reCAPTCHA likewise defers until register / login form interaction — it loads with no consent requirement in most regions, and is consent-gated in EU & UK (TBC), providing no bot protection where consent is ignored/declined.
82	
83	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
84	
85	- The Didomi loader is fetched asynchronously and is small (Didomi-reported figures put it in the low single-digit KB range gzipped).
86	- Per HPC-013/014 the Didomi notice greys out all site content and prevents interaction until the consent flow completes. The underlying LCP candidate (the hero image) still renders behind the scrim, so LCP is measured normally; the page is simply non-interactive until the shopper completes the flow. The grey-out is a confirmed requirement (subject to final designs) — the notice is not deferred away.
87	- All downstream gated scripts are deferred behind their consent callback and dynamically imported / injected. None contribute to the LCP measurement on any page — **with one deliberate, scoped exception: Optimizely Web**. On the US storefront only (per AAB-004), Optimizely is head-loaded before render so its anti-flicker snippet can suppress content flash; this exception is allowed to take priority over the LCP budget. Crazy Egg has no such carve-out and must not block LCP.
88	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to `sdk.privacy-center.org` is emitted in the document head so the SDK fetch does not pay a cold DNS / TLS cost.
89	
90	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
91	
92	- A single Didomi Notice serves all eight storefronts; per-region purpose configuration is managed inside the Didomi Console. The Notice ID does not vary by region — Didomi auto-detects the applicable regulation from the visitor's IP.
93	- Per-region default consent state follows REG-054: EU storefronts opted-out; US domestic requires an explicit choice (no action = opted-out); AU, US international, HK, and ME are opted-in by default. These defaults are configured in the Didomi Console and honoured by the SDK when it loads. The fail-closed rule in §8 applies only when consent state cannot be determined (SDK load failure) and is independent of these per-region defaults.
94	- The marketing opt-in checkbox at registration and newsletter sign-up is **a separate UI control from the Didomi banner** and follows the regional defaults in the Functional Requirements (REG-057): pre-checked on US domestic only, unchecked everywhere else.
95	- The banner language follows the active storefront locale: English for AU, UK, US, HK, ME, and EU international; English, French, Italian, or Spanish for EU domestic. A storefront locale switch triggers `Didomi.setUserLanguage()` so the preference centre also renders in the new language.
96	- **Open (TBD):** consent behaviour on the Global-e-owned checkout iframe origin is not yet settled — how (or whether) Didomi consent state propagates to that cross-origin context remains to be confirmed.
97	
98	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
99	
100	| Failure | Behaviour |
101	|---|---|
102	| Didomi loader fails to fetch (CDN outage, network block, blocker extension) | **Fail closed.** The Didomi Web SDK does not itself default to denied if it fails to load — the storefront implements a 5-second timeout (a project decision, not a Didomi-recommended value). On timeout, the storefront acts as if no consent has been granted: GCM signals stay denied, no gated scripts load. The storefront remains functional for browsing and for SFCC checkout. |
103	| Didomi loader loads but `consent.changed` never fires (SDK initialisation bug, blocked storage) | Same as above — fail closed after the 5-second timeout; the error is logged to monitoring. |
104	| Consent is granted but a downstream script fails to load | The page does not block. The failure is logged. The customer experience continues. |
105	| User revokes consent mid-session | Previously-loaded gated scripts are signalled to disable where the vendor supports it (e.g. GTM `gtag('consent', 'update', …)`). For vendors with no runtime disable, scripts remain in memory but receive no further events; full cleanup happens on the next page navigation. |
106	| User in a region where Didomi has misclassified the regulation | The preference centre is always reachable from the footer "Cookie preferences" link; the customer can adjust manually. |
107	
108	## 9. Open items requiring client confirmation
109	
110	1. **Didomi purpose / vendor IDs.** Provide the Didomi purpose IDs backing the storefront's consent categories (Performance, Analytics, Marketing — REG-051). Also provide Didomi vendor IDs if applicable.
111	2. **Notice IDs per environment.** Zimmermann to provision the Didomi Notices per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod) and supply the Notice IDs so they can be wired into the per-environment configuration. Without these IDs the SDK cannot be exercised end-to-end against a real Didomi configuration.
