1	# 10 — Google reCAPTCHA (Bot Protection)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Google reCAPTCHA v3 provides bot protection on the registration and login forms. The PWA loads the reCAPTCHA script in the browser, collects a token when the customer submits the form, and the MRT layer verifies that token with Google before forwarding the request to SCAPI. The secret key never leaves the server.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- reCAPTCHA v3 script load on the register and login forms (browser)
10	- Token submission alongside form data to the MRT layer
11	- MRT-side token verification against Google's `siteverify` endpoint
12	- Per-region consent gating (EU and UK only)
13	
14	Out of scope of this document:
15	
16	- reCAPTCHA on the gift-card balance-check route — that is an open question (owned separately by the GiveX integration)
17	- reCAPTCHA Enterprise — v3 is the confirmed version
18	
19	## 2. How it works
20	
21	```
22	Customer fills in register / login form
23	        │  (form interaction — reCAPTCHA script loads here, not on page load)
24	        ▼
25	reCAPTCHA v3 runs silently in the background and returns a token
26	        │
27	        ▼
28	Form submits token + credentials to MRT
29	        │
30	        ▼
31	MRT calls Google siteverify:
32	  POST https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify
33	  Body: secret=RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY&response=<token>
34	        │
35	        ├── score low / token invalid → reject; return error to the browser
36	        └── score acceptable         → forward request to SCAPI
37	```
38	
39	- The reCAPTCHA script is loaded **on form interaction only** (not on page load), so it never sits on the critical path for first paint.
40	- The secret key is held as `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (MRT environment variable) and is never exposed in the browser bundle, request URLs, or logs.
41	- The site key (`RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`) is a public identifier, safe to embed in the bundle.
42	
43	## 3. Credentials
44	
45	| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| Site key (`RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`) | Browser — initialises the reCAPTCHA script | Public — bound to the registered domain |
48	| Secret key (`RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`) | MRT environment variable — used server-side for `siteverify` verification | Secret — never reaches the browser |
49	
50	One site key / secret key pair per environment.
51	
52	## 4. Consent and gating
53	
54	- **Most regions:** reCAPTCHA loads on register / login form interaction regardless of Didomi consent state — no consent required.
55	- **EU and UK:** reCAPTCHA is consent-gated — it loads only after Didomi consent is granted. A visitor who declines gets no bot protection on those forms. This is a regulatory trade-off, not a technical limitation.
56	
57	## 5. Performance
58	
59	- The reCAPTCHA script is ~100 KB gzipped. Loading it on form interaction (not page load) means it has zero impact on LCP for any browsing page.
60	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to `www.google.com/recaptcha` and `www.gstatic.com` can be emitted from the register / login route to warm the connection without affecting earlier pages.
61	
62	## 6. Multi-region behaviour
63	
64	| Region | Consent-gated? | Notes |
65	|---|---|---|
66	| AU | No | Loads on form interaction |
67	| US | No | Loads on form interaction |
68	| UK | Yes (EU/UK rule) | Loads only after Didomi consent |
69	| EU domestic | Yes (EU/UK rule) | Loads only after Didomi consent |
70	| EU international | Yes (EU/UK rule) | Loads only after Didomi consent |
71	| HK | No | Loads on form interaction |
72	| ME | No | Loads on form interaction |
73	
74	## 7. Failure modes and graceful degradation
75	
76	| Failure | Behaviour |
77	|---|---|
78	| reCAPTCHA script fails to load (CDN outage, browser extension) | Block form submission; show a "please try again" message. |
79	| MRT `siteverify` call times out or Google returns an error | Block form submission; show a "please try again" message. Log to monitoring. |
80	| Token score is below the acceptable threshold | Treat as a bot; reject silently with a generic error message (do not tell the user why). |
81	| User in EU / UK declines Didomi consent | No reCAPTCHA loads; form submission proceeds without bot protection. No error shown to the user. |
82	
83	## 8. Security
84	
85	- The secret key is never logged, never embedded in the browser bundle, and never passed as a URL query parameter. It is held as an MRT environment variable and used only in the server-side `siteverify` POST body.
86	- Score thresholds are configured in the MRT verification layer (not in reCAPTCHA itself — v3 has no server-side threshold config). The working threshold is 0.5; adjust based on observed production traffic.
87	
88	## 9. Open items requiring client confirmation
89	
90	1. **Per-environment reCAPTCHA site key and secret key.** Zimmermann to provision a Google Cloud project (or use an existing one) and register reCAPTCHA v3 keys for each environment's domain. Supply `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (public) and `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (server-only) per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod). Without these, bot protection cannot be exercised against a real Google account.
91	
92	2. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID (EU and UK storefronts only).** reCAPTCHA is consent-gated in EU and UK (§4). Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers reCAPTCHA (no obvious prior — the purpose is bot protection, not analytics or marketing). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated script loader can be wired correctly. **Owner:** Zimmermann Privacy / Tell No Lies.
93

1	# 11 — Narvar (Estimated Delivery Date Widget)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Narvar provides the pre-purchase and post-purchase delivery experience for SFCC-owned domestic orders. The PWA loads Narvar's pre-purchase widget — **Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT)** — at the checkout delivery-method step to display an Estimated Delivery Date alongside each method (DLV-009, CFD-050). (The technical bundle/API identifiers below retain the "convert" name.)
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) widget initialisation on the checkout delivery-method step
10	- EDD display per delivery method (a range such as "2–4 business days, delivered by Fri 12 Jun")
11	- Suppression of the EDD line when the widget cannot resolve a date or fails to load
12	
13	Out of scope of this document (server-side via SFCC → MuleSoft → Narvar, or out-of-band):
14	
15	- Domestic order confirmation emails (Narvar Notify — triggered from SFCC at order placement, CFD-069)
16	- Shipping confirmation emails (Narvar Notify)
17	- Tracking portal on a Zimmermann-branded subdomain (Narvar-hosted; exact host TBC, linked from emails and My Account)
18	- Returns portal (Narvar Concierge), entered from My Account using billing email plus order number (RRC-005). Narvar owns only the returns *initiation* portal; return history and status shown in My Account are sourced from NewStore via MuleSoft — not from Narvar (RRC-007, RRC-008, RRC-014).
19	- International orders — Narvar is not used for international destinations; Global-e owns international fulfilment messaging
20	
21	## 2. Browser-side architecture
22	
23	```
24	Checkout — delivery method step entered
25	        │
26	        ▼
27	PWA dynamically loads the Narvar CONVERT bundle
28	(deferred behind Didomi Performance consent)
29	        │
30	        ▼
31	PWA calls the CONVERT API with:
32	   retailer ID, shipping postcode, country, line items (SKU, quantity),
33	   order timestamp, available delivery method codes
34	        │
35	        ▼
36	Narvar returns an EDD object per method:
37	   { method: "express", earliestDate, latestDate, businessDays }
38	        │
39	        ▼
40	PWA renders the EDD inline beside each delivery method (CFD-049, CFD-050)
41	```
42	
43	- The CONVERT bundle loads only on the delivery-method step — not on PDP, cart, or any earlier page.
44	- The widget is asynchronous. Delivery methods and costs render immediately from SFCC; the EDD line appears as soon as Narvar responds. Working defaults: 500 ms target, 2-second hard timeout (see §7).
45	- Single delivery method is presented at checkout per DLV-014 — if NewStore later splits the order into multiple shipments, that is communicated post-purchase through Narvar tracking, not at checkout.
46	
47	## 3. Credentials
48	
49	| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
50	|---|---|---|
51	| Narvar retailer ID | Embedded in the CONVERT bundle URL | Public |
52	| CONVERT API key | Embedded client-side; domain-restricted | Public-scoped |
53	
54	One account serves all domestic regions — the retailer ID and CONVERT API key are the same across AU, US, UK, and EU domestic.
55	
56	## 4. Data exchanged
57	
58	| Direction | Data | Notes |
59	|---|---|---|
60	| Browser → Narvar | Postcode, country, line items (SKU, quantity), available delivery method codes, order timestamp | No PII — no name, no email, no street address. For multi-quantity line items, pass unit tax value divided by quantity, not the total line tax (PAY-064). |
61	| Narvar → Browser | EDD range per delivery method | Strings formatted by the storefront for locale. |
62	
63	Per CFD-050 the full street address is not passed to the CONVERT widget — postcode and country are sufficient and minimise PII exposure.
64	
65	## 5. Consent and gating
66	
67	- Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) is loaded under the Performance Didomi consent category (TBC — REG-051 defines the category set; assignment to Performance is a working assumption pending Zimmermann confirmation).
68	- EDD improves the experience but checkout completes without it.
69	- If Performance consent is denied the widget does not load. The storefront shows shipping method names and costs without an EDD line.
70	
71	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
72	
73	- The CONVERT bundle is small (approximately 30 KB gzip — vendor-stated; confirm at integration time). It is loaded with `async` and deferred to the delivery-method step.
74	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Narvar CDN origin is emitted from the cart page so the TLS handshake is warm by the time the widget loads.
75	- The storefront does not block delivery-method rendering on Narvar. The EDD line is a progressive enhancement on top of the SFCC-supplied methods and costs.
76	
77	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
78

1	# 13 — Google Tag Manager on Addingwell (Data Layer, Consent Mode v2, Tag Orchestration)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Google Tag Manager (GTM) is the tag orchestration layer for analytics and marketing on Zimmermann storefronts. The GTM container is **hosted on Addingwell** — a Didomi-owned managed tagging server — so the browser fetches `gtm.js` from a Zimmermann first-party subdomain (`ruffles.zimmermann.com`), not `www.googletagmanager.com`. The tags deployed via GTM (GA4, Meta Pixel, and any other tags Tell No Lies configures) are therefore served through Addingwell.
6	
7	> **Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg are NOT in GTM** (confirmed 2026-06-09). They load as separate **frontend-direct** tags, Didomi-consent-gated, not housed in the GTM container or served via Addingwell.
8	
9	The storefront's responsibility ends at correctly emitting a comprehensive data layer and pointing the loader at the Addingwell tagging-server URL. All downstream tags are loaded, configured, and maintained inside the GTM container by Zimmermann's marketing-technology partner Tell No Lies, who also operates the Addingwell workspace.
10	
11	In scope at the PWA layer:
12	
13	- GTM container loader (`gtm.js`) injection from the Addingwell first-party domain, post-Didomi consent
14	- A native, SFCC-aligned data layer (`window.dataLayer`) populated on every relevant event
15	- Google Consent Mode v2 default and update signal emission, propagated from Didomi to GTM
16	- Enhanced Conversions data — a hashed email at order confirmation (REG-056)
17	
18	Out of scope of this document (owned by Tell No Lies):
19	
20	- All tag configuration inside GTM (which tags fire, with what data, on which triggers)
21	- Downstream vendor scripts loaded via GTM: GA4, Meta Pixel, etc.
22	- Tag-side consent gating beyond what Consent Mode v2 conveys
23	- Experiment definitions in Optimizely; heatmap configuration in Crazy Egg (and the loading of those two scripts, which are frontend-direct tags owned by Tell No Lies — not GTM tags, per the note in §1)
24	
25	The handover boundary is fixed by AAB-001 and AAB-002: Accenture emits the data layer; Tell No Lies consumes it inside GTM.
26	
27	### Responsibilities boundary — Didomi, PWA, Addingwell, GTM, Tell No Lies
28	
29	| Party | Role | PWA relationship |
30	|---|---|---|
31	| **Didomi** (CMP) | Shows the cookie banner, captures consent, and signals which purposes/vendors are allowed. | PWA integrates the `@didomi/react` SDK and gates scripts on its signals. |
32	| **PWA** (storefront) | (1) Always emits the first-party data layer; (2) after Didomi grants consent, loads the GTM container from the Addingwell URL; (3) emits Consent Mode v2 signals derived from Didomi's state. | This is the full PWA scope. |
33	| **Addingwell** (Didomi-owned) | First-party hosting for the GTM container — serves `gtm.js` from a Zimmermann subdomain instead of `googletagmanager.com`. | PWA points the loader at the Addingwell URL; nothing more. |
34	| **GTM container** | Holds and fires GA4, Meta, and other TNL-configured tags. (Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg are NOT in GTM — they are frontend-direct tags; see §1 note.) | Out of PWA scope. |
35	| **Tell No Lies** | Zimmermann's marketing-technology partner; configures the GTM container and operates the Addingwell workspace. | Owns everything downstream of the data layer. |
36	
37	In one line: Didomi = consent; PWA = data layer + Consent Mode + load-GTM-post-consent; Addingwell = first-party hosting for GTM; GTM = the tag container; Tell No Lies = configures it all.
38	
39	## 2. Vendor relationship
40	
41	- **Vendor (orchestration layer):** Google — Google Tag Manager.
42	- **Vendor (hosting):** Addingwell, a Didomi-owned managed server-side GTM platform. The GTM container is hosted on Addingwell; the browser loads it from a Zimmermann first-party subdomain. Container IDs and Addingwell tagging-server URLs are provided to the PWA team by Tell No Lies.
43	- **Container ID (likely single).** Tell No Lies expects a **single GTM container ID** across all environments (to be confirmed — 2026-06-09 call). Any environment separation would be handled via the data layer rather than separate container IDs.
44	
45	## 3. Browser-side architecture
46	
47	```
48	Page load
49	        │
50	        ▼
51	Didomi loads first (strictly necessary) and emits Consent Mode v2 defaults to gtag
52	        gtag('consent', 'default', { ad_storage: 'denied', analytics_storage: 'denied', … })
53	        │
54	        ▼
55	Data layer is populated with first-party SFCC events regardless of consent (AAB-003)
56	        window.dataLayer.push({ event: 'page_view', page: { … } })
57	        │
58	        ▼
59	Didomi resolves the user's consent choice
60	        gtag('consent', 'update', { ad_storage: 'granted', analytics_storage: 'granted', … })
61	        │
62	        ▼
63	GTM container loads from the Addingwell first-party subdomain
64	(`https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/9i683nqysc4y77v.js?awl=M8PJ5D`), when analytics or
65	marketing consent is granted
66	        │
67	        ▼
68	Tell No Lies-configured tags fire per consent state — GA4 collects (with consent),
69	marketing tags only on grant. All tag requests route through Addingwell.
70	```
71	
72	- The data layer is always populated (AAB-003). It is first-party SFCC state — not a third-party script — and never gates on consent.
73	- The GTM container script is served from the Addingwell first-party subdomain and is loaded only after Didomi grants the relevant purpose. Because the request is first-party, it survives most cookie/tracking-prevention browser modes.
74	- Consent Mode v2 defaults are emitted as soon as Didomi reports user state, even before the GTM container loads. This follows Google's recommended pattern and enables Google's cookieless modelling downstream (configured by Tell No Lies).
75	
76	## 4. Authentication and credentials
77	
78	- GTM container ID: **`GTM-M8PJ5D`** — confirmed by Zimmermann 2026-06-10. Public; embedded in the loader.
79	- Addingwell tagging-server URL (`GTM_SERVER_URL`) — public, embedded in the loader. The first-party subdomain is **`ruffles.zimmermann.com`** (confirmed 2026-06-09). It is a Zimmermann-owned subdomain resolving to Addingwell infrastructure (DNS CNAME owned by Zimmermann; TLS cert managed by Addingwell). Per-environment host provisioning is a Zimmermann/Tell No Lies/Addingwell task.
80	- No secret credentials at the storefront layer. The Addingwell workspace API credentials live inside Tell No Lies' Addingwell account, not the PWA bundle.

106	
107	## 5. Data layer schema
108	
109	Per AAB-002, the data layer is the single source of truth. The storefront emits structured events for the lifecycle moments below. Event names follow GA4 e-commerce conventions for compatibility with the most common downstream consumer.
110	
111	> **Unconfirmed — pending Tell No Lies sign-off (open item 3).** The schema below is a proposal based on GA4 conventions and PRD requirements (AAB-002, AAB-004, AAB-005). Tell No Lies must confirm it satisfies the GTM tags before implementation.
112	
113	| Event | When | Key fields |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| `page_view` | Every page load and SPA route change | page type, storefront, locale, customer hash (if logged in), authenticated state, customer group |
116	| `view_item_list` | PLP or search results page | list ID, list name, items[] |

122	| `begin_checkout` | Checkout entry | items[], currency, value |
123	| `add_shipping_info` | Delivery method selected | shipping_tier, items[], currency, value |
124	| `add_payment_info` | Payment method selected | payment_type, items[], currency, value |
125	| `purchase` | Order placed | transaction_id, value, currency, tax, shipping, items[], hashed email (REG-056) |

132

134	- `locale` (en-AU, fr-EU, …)
135	- `currency` (storefront base currency)
136	- `authenticated` (boolean)
137	- `customer_group` (SFCC customer group)
138	- `loyalty_status` (Retail Rewards tier)
139	- `visitor_type` (new vs returning)
140	- `existing_customer` (boolean — returning vs first-time customer, AAB-002)
141	- `lifetime_value` (customer lifetime value, AAB-002)
142	- `device_type` (mobile, tablet, desktop)
143	
144	## 6. Consent Mode v2 mapping (Didomi → gtag)
145	
146	> **Left column unconfirmed.** The Didomi purpose names below are Didomi's standard IAB TCF identifiers. Zimmermann's actual Didomi configuration may use different IDs — verify against the provisioned account once Didomi open item 1 is resolved. The right column (Consent Mode v2 signals) is from Google's official Consent Mode v2 documentation and is authoritative.
147	
148	| Didomi purpose | Consent Mode v2 signal |
149	|---|---|
150	| `measure_audience` / `analytics` | `analytics_storage` |
151	| `select_personalized_ads` / `targeted_advertising` | `ad_storage`, `ad_personalization`, `ad_user_data` |
152	| `personalize_content` | `personalization_storage` |
153	| `functional` | `functionality_storage`, `security_storage` |
154	
155	Defaults emitted before Didomi resolves are all denied (fail-closed). The update is emitted as soon as Didomi reports the user's choice. The `region` parameter on the default `gtag('consent', 'default', …)` call is used where regulation differs (e.g. `region: ['US']` for the US opt-out posture; rest of world is opt-in). The per-region default states themselves are owned by the Didomi configuration.
156	
157	## 7. Performance and loading strategy
158	
159	- The GTM loader script is small and loaded asynchronously, deferred until after Didomi grants the relevant consent. It does not contribute to LCP.
160	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Addingwell first-party hostname (`GTM_SERVER_URL`) is emitted from the document head once consent is granted. No preconnect to `www.googletagmanager.com` is needed — the container is not served from there.
161	
162	## 8. Multi-region behaviour
163	
164	- One GTM container ID across all storefronts (and most likely across all environments too — Tell No Lies to confirm), with region and storefront discrimination via the data layer attributes in §5. This is the assumed Tell No Lies pattern and the simplest model to maintain.
165	- Per-region Consent Mode default states (US opt-out posture vs rest-of-world opt-in posture) are emitted via the `region` parameter on the default `gtag('consent', 'default', …)` call. The actual per-region defaults are configured in the Didomi Console; the storefront translates Didomi state into Consent Mode signals without holding regional logic itself.
166	
167	## 9. Failure modes and graceful degradation
168	
169	| Failure | Behaviour |
170	|---|---|
171	| GTM container fails to load | Storefront unaffected. The data layer continues to populate; tags simply do not fire. |
172	| Didomi never resolves consent | GTM is never loaded; Consent Mode defaults remain denied. Pages work; analytics is absent. |
173	| A downstream tag configured by Tell No Lies errors | Tag-level — does not affect the page. GTM isolates tag failures. |
174	| A data-layer push throws | Every `dataLayer.push` is wrapped in `try / catch`; on failure the storefront logs to monitoring but never blocks the user flow. |
175	
176	## 10. Security and privacy
177	
178	- The hashed email on `purchase` is a SHA-256 hash of the normalised customer email (REG-056). No raw email appears in the data layer. Normalisation follows Google's Enhanced Conversions spec: trim whitespace, lowercase; for `@gmail.com` / `@googlemail.com` addresses additionally remove dots from the local part and strip any `+suffix`.
179	- No PII appears in any data layer event beyond the hashed email. Customer IDs are hashed when present.
180	- No card data ever reaches the data layer. PCI scope is not affected by this integration.
181	
182	## 11. Open items requiring client confirmation
183	
184	1. **Addingwell tagging-server URL (per environment).** The production first-party subdomain is confirmed as `ruffles.zimmermann.com` (2026-06-09). **Zimmermann/Accenture** to provision the equivalent first-party host for each non-production environment (each must be first-party to that environment's storefront domain). The PWA points the loader at this URL.
185	2. **Data layer schema confirmation.** GTM's own tags (GA4, Meta) consume the data layer. The **frontend-direct** Optimizely and Crazy Egg scripts (which are *not* GTM tags — see §1) may also read it, but whether they require any PWA-emitted attributes at all is open (AAB-004 / AAB-005 — Tell No Lies to confirm; may be dropped). Tell No Lies to confirm the event and attribute schema in §5 satisfies the GTM tags, and to confirm whether any additional attributes are needed for Optimizely segmentation (AAB-004) or Crazy Egg filtering (AAB-005).

9	In scope of this document:
10	
11	- Appointment history list rendered inside My Account, read PWA → MRT → Booxi (CRM-165)
12	- The MRT proxy leg that holds the Booxi credential and identifies the customer to Booxi
13	- Embedding, loading, error and retry behaviour observed by the customer in the browser
14	
15	Out of scope of this document:
16	
17	- Appointment **creation, rescheduling, and cancellation** — not in the current PWA scope. Booking is handled in Booxi's own surfaces; the storefront reads history only. If in-storefront booking is later confirmed, it is added here as a separate write path.
18	- Any SFCC or MuleSoft involvement — there is none on this path.
19	
20	## 2. Vendor relationship
21	
22	- **Vendor:** Booxi — appointment scheduling platform; system of record for Zimmermann boutique appointment data (CRM-166).
23	- **PWA's relationship:** Booxi is consumed read-only. The API contract is owned by Booxi / the Zimmermann CRM team; the PWA team is not a co-developer of the API.
24	
25	## 3. Browser-side architecture
26	
27	The flow below is the recommended design. It is not yet a fixed contract — the customer-identification mechanism is pending confirmation with Booxi (see §11), and the specifics below would change if another scheme is agreed.
28	
29	```
30	Browser (My Account → Appointments section)
31	        │  Customer's SLAS access token (JWT) is present after SFCC login
32	        ▼
33	PWA fetches /mobify/proxy/booxi/<endpoint>
34	   Authorization: Bearer <SLAS access token>
35	        │
36	        ▼
37	MRT Node layer:
38	   1. Validates the SLAS JWT signature against SFCC's published JWKS
39	   2. Drops the inbound Authorization header and sets the Booxi credential
40	      header instead (Booxi authenticates via its own `Booxi-PartnerKey`
41	      header, not a bearer `Authorization` header)
42	   3. Resolves the customer's Booxi identity (see §4) and scopes the request to it
43	   4. Forwards to https://<booxi-host>/<endpoint>
44	        │
45	        ▼
46	Booxi API:
47	   • Authorises the request via the Booxi API credential
48	   • Returns the customer's appointment history
49	        │
50	        ▼
51	Booxi response → MRT → Browser (typed JSON, only the fields the section needs)
52	```
53	
54	- The browser never carries the Booxi credential. The Booxi API credential is held as an MRT environment variable and is appended only on the MRT → Booxi leg.
55	- The appointments section is read-only and authenticated — it renders only for a logged-in customer on the My Account route.
56	- The section is built as a self-contained module so it can be enabled when Booxi is ready without restructuring the surrounding My Account page (CRM-167).
57	
58	## 4. Authentication and credentials
59	
60	| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
61	|---|---|---|
62	| Booxi Partner API key (sent in the `Booxi-PartnerKey` header) | MRT environment variable; injected by MRT before forwarding | Secret — Booxi mandates this key is used server-side only and never reaches the browser |
63	| Customer SLAS access token (JWT) | Forwarded from the browser to MRT; used by MRT to authenticate the customer | Sensitive — proves user identity |
64	| SFCC JWKS | Used by MRT to verify the SLAS JWT signature | Public |
65	
66	- **No Booxi credential in the browser bundle.** The Booxi credential is held server-side as an MRT environment variable, appended on the MRT → Booxi leg only.
67	- **Customer identification (open — see §11).** The PWA must prove *which* customer's appointments to return without letting the browser request an arbitrary customer's data. The recommended approach is that MRT validates the customer's SLAS JWT and resolves the corresponding Booxi customer reference server-side (from a Booxi customer ID held on the SFCC/Omneo profile, or via a Booxi lookup), then scopes the request to that reference. MRT must never accept a raw Booxi customer ID, email, or appointment ID from the browser as the identity input.
68	- One Booxi API credential per environment. Rotation cadence and named owner are tracked in §11.
69	
70	## 5. Data exchanged
71	
72	| Direction | Data | Notes |
73	|---|---|---|
74	| Browser → MRT | Customer JWT (SLAS access token); endpoint path | The browser never sees the Booxi credential and never passes a customer identifier as input. |
75	| MRT → Booxi | Booxi API credential; customer-scoped identifier resolved server-side | The credential authorises the channel; the resolved identity scopes the data. |
76	| Booxi → MRT → Browser | Typed JSON — appointment history (date/time, boutique, appointment type, status) | MRT projects only the fields the My Account section renders. |
77	
78	The customer sees only their own appointment data, which they already own. No payment data is involved on this path.
79	
80	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
81	
82	- The appointment history read fires only when the My Account appointments section is in view — it does not preload on the dashboard or any other route.
83	- TanStack Query caches the appointment history response on the client; stale data is acceptable for history display.
84	- The My Account appointments module is route-level code-split so it adds nothing to other route bundles, and so it can ship dark until Booxi is enabled (CRM-167).
85	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Booxi host is emitted from the My Account routes once the customer is authenticated and the section is enabled.
86	
87	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
88	
89	- Appointments are boutique-bound; the history list reflects whichever boutiques the customer has booked with, independent of the storefront locale.
90	- A single Booxi tenant is assumed across all eight storefronts; per-region boutique availability is configured in Booxi, not in the PWA.
91	- Locale affects only the display formatting of dates and labels in the storefront, not the Booxi request.
92	
93	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
94	
95	Each external system must fail independently — a Booxi outage must not break the My Account page.
96	
97	| Failure | Behaviour |
98	|---|---|
99	| MRT cannot verify the SLAS JWT (expired, invalid) | Return 401 to the browser without calling Booxi. The storefront triggers a silent SLAS refresh and retries; if refresh fails, force re-login. |
100	| Booxi 5xx or timeout on the history read | Suppress the appointments section (or show a compact "appointments temporarily unavailable" state with a retry CTA) rather than throwing. The rest of My Account renders normally. Never block the page on Booxi. |
101	| Customer has no appointment history | Render an explicit empty state, not an error. |
102	| Customer is unauthenticated on the route | Standard My Account authentication redirect. No Booxi request is issued. |
103	| Booxi rotates or revokes the API credential | Rotation is handled in the MRT environment configuration by the integration team. No browser-side change required. |
104	
105	## 9. Security and privacy
106	
107	- The Booxi API credential is held as an MRT environment variable and never appears in browser JavaScript, request URLs, or logs. MRT redacts the Authorization header in its access logs.
108	- The customer's SLAS JWT is forwarded to MRT only over TLS 1.2+ and is not forwarded to Booxi as a raw identity token — MRT resolves the customer-scoped Booxi reference server-side so the browser cannot request another customer's data.
109	- No appointment identifier or customer reference is accepted from the browser as an input to the request.
110	- The browser calls the same-origin MRT proxy path (`/mobify/proxy/booxi/...`) — no CSP `connect-src` entry for Booxi's host is needed; MRT makes the server-side call to Booxi outside the browser's CSP boundary.
111	- On a right-to-erasure request (REG-060–067), removal of appointment data in Booxi is handled by the CRM/integration team through Booxi's own erasure process; the storefront has no separate erasure flow for Booxi data.
112	
113	## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation
114	
115	1. **Storefront scope (CRM-165 – CRM-167).** Confirm whether the My Account appointments surface is read-only history (current assumption) or whether in-storefront booking / rescheduling / cancellation is also in scope. Until confirmed, the section is built read-only and structured to slot in without redesign.
116	2. **Booxi API specification.** Booxi to publish the API contract for appointment history — endpoint(s), request and response schemas, the appointment status values and their customer-facing copy, error codes, and pagination. The PWA-side types are generated from this contract.
117	3. **Customer-identification mechanism (PWA-direct path).** Confirm how the storefront proves customer identity to Booxi without allowing the browser to retrieve an arbitrary customer's appointments. Confirm whether a Booxi customer ID is stored on the SFCC/Omneo profile (and how it is populated), or whether MRT must look the customer up in Booxi at request time. The mechanism must prevent impersonation.
118	4. **Per-environment Booxi credentials.** Booxi to supply, per environment: Booxi API host, API credential, and the credential rotation cadence and named owner. Note the API host is region-specific (e.g. a North America vs EU base URL), so confirm which regional host serves Zimmermann.

1	# 05 — GiveX (Gift Cards)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	GiveX is Zimmermann's gift card and credit note processor. This document covers the PWA surfaces that directly call GiveX via MRT:
6	
7	- The **balance-check input** in My Account (GC-051–062) and the "Check Balance" link in the checkout gift card entry field (GC-037). Both use the same MRT endpoint: `POST /mobify/proxy/mulesoft/givex/balance`.
8	- The **gift card purchase experience** (§12) — the PWA renders the product, denomination selector, and gift-details form, and persists them on the basket. GiveX issuance is server-side and is not a PWA-direct call.
9	
10	Out of scope (server-side, not a PWA-direct path):
11	
12	- Gift card and credit note validate / redeem / refund at checkout (GC-034–049) — handled via the NewStore adaptor → MuleSoft → GiveX. The PWA sees only the resulting payment-instrument state from SCAPI.
13	- Gift card issuance at purchase — SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore → GiveX.
14	- GiveX validate / redeem / refund webhooks exposed to Global-e (PRC-44).
15	- Reversal on capture failure — handled server-side by NewStore / SFCC.
16	
17	## 2. Vendor relationship
18	
19	GiveX is reached via MuleSoft — the PWA never holds a GiveX credential or makes a direct GiveX call. For the balance check, MuleSoft owns the GiveX socket, host failover, and credentials internally; the PWA calls MuleSoft over HTTPS. Redemption at checkout goes via the NewStore adaptor through MuleSoft, outside the PWA boundary.
20	
21	## 3. PWA-layer architecture
22	
23	```
24	My Account (GC-051) / Checkout "Check Balance" link (GC-037)
25	        │
26	        ▼
27	Customer enters gift card or credit note number and PIN
28	        │
29	        ▼
30	Browser: POST /mobify/proxy/mulesoft/givex/balance
31	   body: { number, pin }
32	        │
33	        ▼
34	MRT Node layer:
35	   1. Applies rate-limit and bot protection on this route
36	      (no per-customer cap — GC-062 — but route is hardened
37	       with WAF / bot management / rate-limit / CAPTCHA per
38	       GiveX security guidance)
39	   2. Forwards over HTTPS to MuleSoft with the MuleSoft API token
40	      held as an MRT environment variable
41	        │
42	        ▼
43	MuleSoft → GiveX (internal — MuleSoft's responsibility)
44	        │
45	        ▼
46	MuleSoft → MRT → Browser:
47	   { maskedNumber, balance, currency, expiry, error? }
48	        │
49	        ▼
50	PWA renders the result inline beside the input (GC-054, GC-055)
51	```
52	
53	The browser never sees a GiveX credential or raw GiveX error. It sees only an HTTPS request to the storefront's own MRT origin and a typed JSON response.
54	
55	Both the My Account balance check and the checkout Check Balance link (GC-037) use the same MRT endpoint. Login is not required for either (GC-059).
56	
57	The balance check requires both the card number and its PIN, for both gift cards and credit notes. Zimmermann's GiveX merchant program has secure PINs enabled, so the PIN field is mandatory on every request. The PIN is a payment credential — see §9.
58	
59	The customer can check another card or credit note without leaving the page (GC-055). The same input field accepts both gift card and credit note numbers (GC-057).
60	
61	## 4. Authentication and credentials
62	
63	| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
64	|---|---|---|
65	| MuleSoft API token | MRT environment variable; injected on outbound request | Secret — never reaches the browser |
66	
67	The customer is not required to be authenticated (GC-059). The call is not bound to a SLAS JWT.
68	
69	## 5. Data exchanged
70	
71	| Direction | Data | Notes |
72	|---|---|---|
73	| Browser → MRT | Card or credit note number and PIN — POST body only, never a query string | Both are payment credentials; not logged, not stored beyond the request |
74	| MRT → MuleSoft | Number, PIN, and MuleSoft API token | HTTPS |
75	| MuleSoft → MRT → Browser | Masked card serial, balance, currency, expiry, mapped error code | Only the serial portion is returned; prefix and check digit are dropped by MuleSoft |
76	
77	The full card number and PIN are treated as payment credentials and are handled as described in §9.
78	
79	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
80	
81	- The route is reached only when the customer submits the form — no upfront script load.
82	- Working performance target: p95 under 1.5 seconds including the GiveX round-trip via MuleSoft. Hard timeout at 5 seconds (§8).
83	
84	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
85	
86	- The balance check is available on all storefronts — domestic and international (GC-051–062 scope).
87	- Currency in the response is whatever GiveX returns for the card. The storefront formats it per the active locale without converting.
88	
89	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
90	
91	| Failure | Behaviour |
92	|---|---|
93	| GiveX does not recognise the card number | Display the error from GiveX (GC-056) — no inline pre-submission validation. |
94	| Card expired or zero balance | Show the appropriate error message (GC-060). |
95	| MuleSoft returns an error after exhausting failover | "Balance check is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly." (GC-061). Shopper can retry; subject to rate-limit. |
96	| MRT timeout above 5 seconds | Same handling as MuleSoft error above. |
97	| Rate-limit triggered | Generic retry-later message. Do not disclose the threshold. |
98	| Bot-management challenge fires | The route presents the challenge before forwarding to MuleSoft. |
99	
100	## 9. Security and privacy
101	
102	- Card number and PIN are submitted in the POST body only — never as a URL query string. Query strings appear in MRT access logs, browser history, and Referer headers.
103	- No `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, or cookie may hold the full card number or PIN. Form state lives in React only and is cleared on unmount.
104	- No `console.log`, Sentry breadcrumb, GTM dataLayer push, or analytics event may contain the card number or PIN. The logger and Sentry `beforeSend` must include a redaction rule for this route. No body-logging middleware on the balance-check route.
105	- After submission, render only the serial portion (e.g. `••••••••1234`). MuleSoft strips the prefix and check digit before the response reaches MRT.
106	- The MRT balance-check route applies WAF, bot management, rate-limit, and CAPTCHA, because the underlying MuleSoft credential is merchant-level rather than per-shopper. There is no per-customer cap (GC-062); per-IP and per-session limits are enforced at the edge.
107	
108	## 10. Gift card purchase (PWA surface)
109	
110	The storefront sells gift cards as products. The PWA renders the PDP, denomination selector, and gift-details form, and persists gift metadata on the basket. GiveX issuance is server-side after payment capture — the PWA makes no GiveX call on this path.
111	
112	**Scope (confirmed):**
113	- Purchase — domestic storefronts only at launch; international purchase is a future roadmap item.
114	- Redemption (using a gift card as payment) — domestic storefronts only; not at Global-e international checkout at launch (GC-050).
115	- Balance check — all storefronts (GC-059).
116	
117	**Two products:** Physical and digital gift cards are separate SFCC product IDs. Physical cards ship; digital cards send an email to the recipient.
118	
119	**Fixed denominations:** $100, $200, $250, $300, $500. Selected via a searchable dropdown (GC-001–004). The PWA renders the selector from SCAPI product data — the set can change without a code change.
120	
121	**Gift details captured at add-to-cart:** sender name, recipient name, recipient email, delivery date, optional personal message (GC-001, GC-003). The PWA validates recipient email format, delivery date within 3 months, and personal-message length (GC-005–007).
122	
123	**Data flow:** Gift metadata is attached to the basket line item as custom attributes via SCAPI. The PWA persists the metadata and does not call GiveX.
124	
125	**PII:** Recipient name and email are third-party personal data. Carried over HTTPS, not logged beyond SFCC requirements, and subject to the standard data-handling posture.
126	
127	## 11. Open items requiring client confirmation
128	
129	1. **MuleSoft balance-check HTTPS contract.** MuleSoft to publish the request and response schema for the balance-check endpoint (including the card number and PIN fields), the error taxonomy mapping GiveX failure codes to the GC-042 / GC-060 / GC-061 customer-facing messages, and the invalid-PIN case. Without this contract the call cannot be implemented against a real MuleSoft instance.
130	2. **Per-environment MuleSoft endpoint, API token, and rate-limit thresholds.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: MuleSoft host, balance-check endpoint path, MuleSoft API token, and the agreed per-IP / per-session rate-limit thresholds and the bot-management vendor in front of the MRT route.
131	3. **Whether the balance-check route uses a CAPTCHA.** Confirm whether the MRT route should present a CAPTCHA challenge when the bot manager elevates a request. If yes, the simplest option is Google reCAPTCHA v3, reusing the site key already provisioned for register / login. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

1	# 02 — Contentful (CMS)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Reading published content via the Delivery API
10	- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
11	- Live preview in Contentful Studio
12	- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
13	- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
14	- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries
15	
16	Out of scope of this document:
17	
18	- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
19	- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
20	- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)
21	
22	**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).
23	
24	| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
25	|---|---|---|---|
26	| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
27	| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
28	| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
29	| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
30	| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
31	| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
32	| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
33	| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
34	| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |
35	
36	## 2. Content type management (build-time)
37	
38	Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:
39	
40	- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
41	- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
42	- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.
43	
44	## 3. Browser-side architecture
45	
46	```
47	PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
48	        │
49	        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
50	        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
51	        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
52	        │
53	        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
54	        │        Editor preview only. Token set in MRT as an env var
55	        │        on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod).
56	        │        Reached client-side on the /preview route and via
57	        │        ?preview on Experience pages — both are gated: if no
58	        │        CPA token is present, both paths fail explicitly with
59	        │        a 404 and are noindex (no delivery fallback). The Live
60	        │        Preview SDK requires the token in the browser for
61	        │        postMessage-based real-time updates.
62	        │
63	        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
64	        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
65	        │
66	        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
67	                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
68	                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
69	```
70	
71	- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
72	- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
73	- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the `/preview` route renders the entry inside Studio's iframe. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK subscribes to `postMessage` events from Studio for real-time content updates. The CPA token is used client-side here — this is required by the SDK and is acceptable because: (a) the token is set only on dev/test/sit/uat (never staging or prod) MRT environments, (b) the route returns a 404 when no preview token is present, and (c) the route is `noindex`. The MRT proxy approach was considered but deferred in favour of the simpler client-side SDK integration.
74	- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.
75	
76	## 4. Authentication and credentials
77	
78	| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
79	|---|---|---|
80	| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
81	| Preview API token (CPA) | `/preview` route and `?preview` on Experience pages (dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging or prod) | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. Set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only; never set on staging or prod. Both the `/preview` route and `?preview` Experience pages return 404 and are `noindex` when the token is absent — they fail explicitly, with no delivery fallback. Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (required for postMessage updates). |
82	| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
83	| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |
84	
85	Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.
86	
87	## 5. Data exchanged
88	
89	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
90	|---|---|---|
91	| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
92	| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
93	| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
94	| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
95	| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |
96	
97	No PII flows through Contentful.
98	
99	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
100	
101	- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
102	- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
103	- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
104	- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
105	- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
106	- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.
107	
108	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
109	
110	- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
111	- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
112	- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.
113	
114	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
115	
116	| Failure | Behaviour |
117	|---|---|
118	| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
119	| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
120	| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
121	| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
122	| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
123	| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
124	| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |
125	
126	## 9. Security and privacy

46	## Tier 1 Approval — How It's Actually Enforced
47	
48	Claude Code's confirmation prompt before touching a Tier 1 file (Hard Rule #2) is a workflow
49	safeguard, not the security boundary — it can't be, since it only governs what Claude itself
50	does, not what any other tool or a direct `git push` can do. The real enforcement is server-side:
51	
52	- [CODEOWNERS](../CODEOWNERS) routes every Tier 1 path to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`, a
53	  real GitHub org team.
54	- Branch protection on `develop`/`main`/`release/**` requires an approving code-owner review
55	  before merge — this is the actual gate, enforced natively by GitHub with no Actions
56	  involvement, so it can't be affected by a broken or delayed CI run.
57	- `.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml`'s `tier1-guard` job posts a loud warning and an
58	  owner-contact-map on any PR touching a Tier 1 path. It is **not** a required status check —
59	  GitHub locked down cross-run check-run updates in Feb 2025, which made a "hard-fail until
60	  approved, then flip to pass on review" required check impossible to implement reliably (a
61	  fresh commit is needed to re-evaluate it, since a later review can't flip an earlier run's
62	  result). The CODEOWNERS-based review requirement above is the real, working block.
63	
64	Because the actual gate lives in GitHub, not in Claude's judgement, this file does not encode
65	personal names or email addresses as a bypass condition — a string in a shared, version-controlled
66	file is not an identity check; anyone (or any other Claude session) could satisfy it by typing it.
67	Instead, Claude may verify the real, authenticated identity behind the current session:
68	
69	- Before pausing to ask for Tier 1 confirmation, run `gh api user --jq .login`, then check
70	  `gh api orgs/ZimmermannAU/teams/tier-1-approvers/members --jq '.[].login'` (or check for `admin`
71	  via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/collaborators/<login>/permission`). If that GitHub
72	  login is a member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` or holds repo admin, Claude may proceed
73	  with the edit after stating which Tier 1 file is being touched and why — no separate
74	  confirmation message is required, since GitHub already recognises that account as an approver.
75	- If the authenticated login is **not** a member/admin, Claude must still stop per Hard Rule #2:
76	  name the file, and require the developer to secure an approving review from
77	  `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` before the PR can merge. CODEOWNERS auto-requests that review
78	  and branch protection blocks the merge without it, regardless of what `tier1-guard` reports.
79	- This check only ever reduces _how many times Claude pauses to ask_. It changes nothing about
80	  what GitHub will actually allow to merge — that's deliberate, so a compromised or careless
81	  Claude session can't grant itself write access to a frozen file.
82	
83	## Coding Task Workflow
84	
85	Every coding task follows these four steps in order. Do not skip ahead — pause at the marked points and wait for the user.
86	
87	1. **Clarify requirements.** Identify every gap, ambiguity, or contradiction in the request and the relevant `.docs/`. Confirm each one with the user before moving on — no assumptions. See Hard Rule #12: ask one question at a time.
88	2. **Plan.** State the files you intend to touch, _why_ each one is being touched, and any base template files that will need to be copied to `overrides/`. Then **pause** and wait for the user to confirm the plan. See the **Minimal changes** rule below.
89	3. **Copy first (if any).** For every base template file identified in step 2, follow the **Copy-first rule** in the Rules section. Then **pause** and let the user test and stage the override files before any functional changes.
90	4. **Implement.** Make the planned modifications. Remove the `console.log` markers from step 3 once the user confirms the overrides are rendering. Before committing a non-trivial code change, run a local CodeRabbit review: confirm the CLI is installed and authenticated (`coderabbit auth status`; if not authenticated, `coderabbit auth login --api-key "$CODERABBIT_API_KEY"` — see `.env.sample`), then `cr review --light --base develop` (use `main` instead on a `release/**`/`hotfix/**` branch). **The CLI is required, not optional** — if it isn't installed or authenticated, stop and have the developer install it (https://www.coderabbit.ai/cli) and run `npm run env -- init` to pull the shared key, rather than committing without a local review. The review itself is still advisory relative to the actual merge gate (the GitHub PR review remains the real gate) — use judgement on whether a flagged finding is worth fixing before the commit vs. leaving it for the PR review to catch, but the review must actually run.
91	
92	**Responding to a CodeRabbit PR review.** Once CodeRabbit finishes reviewing an open PR, always leave an explicit in-thread reply for every finding, whether it's fixed or not — CodeRabbit's learning feature picks up patterns from PR conversation, so silence teaches it nothing and an explanation teaches it to stop flagging the same non-issue. A fix commit alone, with no reply posted on the thread, doesn't count. For a finding that gets fixed, a short in-thread reply confirming the fix (referencing the commit is fine) is enough. For a finding that is *not* being fixed because it conflicts with this repo's own rules/docs/architecture (e.g. a Tier 1 exception that was actually followed correctly, an intentional design tradeoff already recorded in `.docs/`) — reply in-thread explaining the specific rule or doc that justifies not changing it, so CodeRabbit's learning has the context to recognise the same pattern next time instead of re-flagging it. Never silently dismiss a finding without a reply.
93	
94	## When to Stop and Ask a Human
95	
96	| Trigger                                                                      | Action                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
97	| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
98	| Task requires a Tier 1 file                                                  | Check the authenticated `gh` identity against `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`/admin (see [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced)). If verified, name the file and proceed. Otherwise stop and require named owner approval. |
99	| A shared hook needs its function signature changed                           | Stop. Requires a team RFC.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
100	| A new package dependency is needed                                           | Stop. Integration team must approve.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
101	| Current branch is `develop` or `main`                                        | Stop immediately. No changes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
102	| Change affects more than one regional site config                            | Stop. Integration team sign-off required.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
103	| Change spans multiple protection tiers                                       | Stop. Confirm scope with the developer before continuing.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
104	| Requirement is missing, ambiguous, contradictory, or unconfirmed in `.docs/` | Stop. Flag, propose, wait for approval (see Requirements section).                                                                                                                                                                                  |
105	
106	## Multi-site & Routing
107	
108	The SFCC sites are hard routing and config boundaries — **never bleed config across sites.** Never assume a storefront's routing, URL prefix, checkout ownership, or consent defaults without checking [.docs/prd/regional.md](.docs/prd/regional.md).
109	
110	## Commands
111	
112	- `npm start` — local dev at http://localhost:3000. **Do not run!** Ask the user to restart if needed.
113	- `npm run build`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run push` (Managed Runtime deploy)
114	
115	## Accessibility
116	
117	Target WCAG 2.2 AA. Fall back to 2.1 AA only where 2.2 is technically infeasible — document why.
118	
119	## Rules
120	
121	*Day-to-day code-writing conventions live in `.claude/rules/` and load automatically:
122	[conventions.md](.claude/rules/conventions.md) (cross-cutting: naming, imports, DRY, security),
123	[typescript.md](.claude/rules/typescript.md) (TS idioms), [css.md](.claude/rules/css.md)
124	(Chakra tokens, `.scss`), and [components.md](.claude/rules/components.md)
125	(component/hook/utility structure, Storybook categorisation, composition). The rules below
126	are project-specific behaviours and security guardrails that don't fit there.*
127	
128	- **No mocking:** All data must come from the live Commerce Cloud API via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hooks. No MSW or hardcoded fixtures in production paths.
129	- **Environment variables:** Never hardcode secrets, tokens, API keys, or credentials anywhere in the codebase. Local values live in `.env.shared` (tier-independent) and `.env.<tier>` (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod) — gitignored, managed via `npm run env` (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`; full command reference in `.env.sample`'s header) — and are set as platform environment variables on Managed Runtime for staging/prod. When adding a new env var: (1) add it to `.env.sample` tagged `# scope:shared|tier|personal|auto` on its own comment line above the key (value only if it's a non-secret public identifier, otherwise leave blank — never a trailing comment, or a blank placeholder reads as non-empty to the pre-commit secret guard), (2) run `npm run env -- init` to scaffold the new key into `.env.shared`/`.env.<tier>`, then fill in the real value locally. Never put tokens, bearer credentials, DSNs, or licence keys in `.env.sample`. Non-personal shared/tier values may additionally be centrally published via `npm run env -- push <scope>` (tier-1-approvers only) to this repo's GitHub Environments — genuinely personal credentials (`scope:personal`, e.g. your own Atlassian or Contentful CMA token) must never be pushed.
130	- **Comments:** Do not remove existing commented-out code or comments (except when removing the corresponding code) — leave for the user to delete manually. (For _new_ comments introduced in a PR, see conventions.md.)
131	- **Icons:** Use `overrides/app/components/icons` — this is the single source of truth for all icons (Zimmermann custom and base PWA). Do not import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons` directly. If a required icon is missing from the overrides set, ask the user — do not substitute a visually different one.
132	- **Styling:** Chakra UI component props first; use a `.scss` file alongside the component only when Chakra props are insufficient. The `overrides/app/theme/` folder is the source of truth — brand tokens in `foundation/` (Tier 1), one file per component override in `components/` (Tier 2), composed in `index.ts`. Register a new component override in `theme/components/index.ts`.
133	- **Minimal changes:** Make the smallest change that fully achieves the task. Do not remove or replace existing base template functionality unless explicitly instructed. When a larger change (e.g., a refactor for cleanliness) seems beneficial, propose it and wait for user confirmation — never do it silently.
134	- **Copy-first rule:** For any task that requires overriding base template files that do not yet exist in `overrides/`, the very first step is to prepare all of them at once: (1) copy each file from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`, (2) convert each to TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`) and update relevant imports, (3) run `npx tsc --noEmit`, (4) add a temporary `console.log` to each copied file identifying it (e.g. `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')`) so the user can verify the override is rendering instead of the base component, then **stop and present the converted files to the user to test**. Wait for the user to confirm the overrides are rendering before making any functional changes; remove the `console.log` statements once confirmed. Never skip this step or bundle it silently with functional changes.
135	
136	## Consent & Marketing
137	
138	- **Didomi:** Do not load any third-party script until Didomi consent is granted. Gate all analytics, marketing, and tracking scripts behind Didomi callbacks.
139	- **Marketing opt-in:** Unchecked by default on all storefronts except US (pre-checked). Sync opt-in state: FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys.
140	
141	_Per-storefront Didomi defaults, GTM/Enhanced Conversions setup, and Inside Chat rules: see [.docs/prd/regional.md](.docs/prd/regional.md)._
142	
143	## Type Definitions
144	
145	- **Component-specific prop types:** co-locate at the top of the component file.
146	- **Shared types** (Commerce Cloud entities, API responses, shared hook signatures): `overrides/app/types/` — split into `commerce.ts`, `components.ts`, `hooks.ts`, re-exported via `index.ts`.
147	- Don't re-declare types already exported by `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` or `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` — import them directly.
148	
149	## Testing
150	
151	Three layers: **Vitest** (unit logic) · **Storybook** `play` (component interactions) · **Playwright** (E2E). Write tests only where failure would be non-obvious or costly to debug — data mapping, integration boundaries, complex state, and pure logic that would survive a refactor invisibly if broken. Every UI component needs a `.stories.tsx`; every logic-heavy feature needs a `.test.ts` or a story `play`.
152	
153	Full layer guidance, file layout, selector priority, and mocking policy: [.claude/rules/testing.md](.claude/rules/testing.md). (The no-MSW rule in Rules applies to production paths only.)
154	
155	## Graceful Degradation
156	
157	Each external system must fail independently — one outage must not break the whole page. Two defaults override any per-system behaviour: **fail closed on consent** (if consent state is unknown, load no third-party scripts), and **never silently substitute a different checkout, payment, or commerce flow** when an integration is down — surface an explicit error instead.
158	
159	## Performance
160	
161	Mobile page speed is a top priority. Every change that touches rendering, data fetching, or assets must not regress it.
162	
163	- **LCP budget is tight (≤ 2s at p75 mobile)** — Defer every third-party script that isn't required for first paint. Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM, Optimizely, Inside Chat, Narvar EDD, reCAPTCHA, etc.) must not block LCP — use `defer`, `async`, or post-hydration injection. If a new third-party integration looks like it might land on the critical path, flag it before merging.
164	- **Images:** Always use lazy loading and serve correctly sized images. Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
165	- **Code splitting:** Prefer dynamic `import()` for heavy components not needed on initial render.
166	- **Data fetching:** Avoid over-fetching — request only the fields you need. Waterfall requests are not acceptable; parallelise where possible.
167	- **Bundle size:** Do not introduce large dependencies without confirming with the user.
168	- **Dependencies:** Before implementing any feature that may require a third-party library, check `package.json` for what is already installed. Evaluate whether an existing dependency can satisfy the requirement. If a better third-party option exists, present the recommendation (existing vs. new, with trade-offs) and wait for user approval before installing anything.
169	
170	## Gotchas
171	
172	- **Theme runtime errors:** Custom components (e.g. `ListMenu`) must be defined in the theme object or destructuring will throw.
173	- **Commerce SDK types not importable:** Check `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/dist/` for generated definitions, or declare a narrow local `type`.
174	- **Magento password migration:** Passwords were not migrated from Magento — all existing customers must reset at go-live. Do not assume any saved credentials exist. Account creation and login flows must handle this gracefully (CFD-013).
175	
176	## Requirements
177	
178	Requirements for this project are in `.docs/`, they must be strictly followed.
179	Before any code changes, verify logic against relevant `.docs/` files.
180	For any task that touches an external integration, check the matching `.docs/integration/NN-*.md` doc.
181	
182	If a requirement is missing, ambiguous, or not yet confirmed — **stop, flag the ambiguity, propose a solution, and wait for user approval before proceeding.** Do not fill gaps with assumptions.
183	
184	Verification: Start every task by briefly stating which doc/section you are following (e.g. "Implementing per auth.md section 2.1" or "Implementing per 07-adyen.md §3").
185	
186	**Doc integrity:** Confirmed PRDs (`.docs/prd/`) and finalised Figma designs are the source of truth for _requirements_. `.docs/integration/` docs are guides for _how_ each integration works technically. If a user instruction contradicts either, pause immediately — cite the specific doc, section, and requirement ID — and ask the user whether the doc should be updated or the instruction is a deliberate override. Do not proceed silently either way. The same applies if you spot any improvement or conflict within the docs themselves.
187	
188	## Living Memory
189	
190	`.docs/memory/` is the project's persistent memory. Read [.docs/memory/projectState.md](.docs/memory/projectState.md) at the start of every session (or run `/session-start`). For what belongs in each memory file and when to update it, see the [session-start skill](.claude/skills/session-start/SKILL.md).
191	
192	**Open items that block implementation** are listed under "Unresolved Dependencies" in [.docs/memory/projectState.md](.docs/memory/projectState.md). Ask the user before hard-coding assumptions about any of them.
193	
194	---
195	
196	_Human-developer onboarding now lives on Confluence: [Claude Code CLI — Developer Onboarding Guide](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/304775192) (session checklist, prompting guide), [1.2 Team Overview](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/261586947) (contacts), and [Claude Code Skills Reference](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/297959425) (useful skills) — not loaded into Claude's context._
197	
198	---

Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
79	  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.
80	  - **Tooling — safe to build now, doesn't touch governance docs:**
81	    1. `npm version` adoption — no code change needed, it's a built-in npm command; just start using it per the Confluence page's "How to deploy" section instead of raw `git tag`. First tag will be `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
82	    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
83	    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."

Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.

86	  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
